title: Crate, binary and environment are named jevify
description:
The crate, the binary, the environment variables and every identifier the program prints are named `jevify`, as if no other name ever existed. No alias, no second binary, no fallback to old variable names, no compatibility shim.

Write set: Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock (through cargo, not by hand), src/**, tests/**, scripts/**, benchmarks/bench.sh, demo-record.sh, demo.tape, demo.cast, dist-workspace.toml, .github/workflows/*.yml, .claude-plugin/**, plugins/** (move plugins/grevi to plugins/jevify and the inner skills/grevi to skills/jevify with `git mv`, then edit the content), deny.toml and .gitleaks.toml if they name the project. Not in this bead: README.md, PRIVACY.md, CHANGELOG.md, AGENTS.md, docs/**, benchmarks/*.md, evals/**/*.md, .beads/.

Details: package name and binary `jevify`; clap `name`; QUICK_START and every help text; error and stderr prefixes (`jevify:`); `GREVI_*` variables become `JEVIFY_*` everywhere including tests/common and capabilities; the cache and config directory name; the HTTP user agent; `scripts/release.sh` (repo `tpellet/jevify`, crate URL); `publish-crates.yml` (package name); `release.yml` is generated by cargo-dist, so regenerate it with the pinned `dist` when it is installed, otherwise edit by hand and say so in the report; `tests/release.rs` and any test that asserts names. The version stays 0.3.4; the lead bumps it at release. Manual edits only (Edit tool, per file); no sed, perl or scripts over code files.

Gate: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo check --all-targets`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test -- --test-threads=1`; `rg -i grevi` over the write set returns nothing; `./target/debug/jevify capabilities --json` names no old identifier. `docs/ROBOT_MODE.md` and `PRIVACY.md` are compiled into the binary and belong to the docs bead: if a test fails only because of their text, report it instead of editing them.

title: Preserve non-secret identifiers and changes during redaction
description: Live audit hunch-q3i found add abstains on an explicit token-expiry change. Optional separators in SECRET regex match ordinary identifier suffixes. title: Semantic operands: put meaning into the arguments of any command
description:
Vision (owner, 2026-09-20): put meaning into the operands of any command. A command line is head, flags, operands. `run` fills the head by meaning from PATH and man pages. This epic fills operands by meaning from real objects: the user writes the command, grevi replaces a description with an existing handle (a path by default; a branch, a commit, a process for commands that take those). The grammar is user-written and every value exists, so "point, never generate" holds.

    grevi code "where man pages are parsed"
    grevi git switch "payment timeout fix"
    grevi pytest "the tests about token expiry"

Boundaries found in design review:
- `add` stays a verb: it stages hunks, and a path-level `git add` would stage unrelated hunks of the same file.
- `why`, `is`, `pick`, `filter` are the output side and are already universal through a pipe.
- The governing plan says unvalidated command grammar remains a proposal, and `run` executes only zero-argument true, false, pwd, ls. Executing a user-written argv with substituted handles needs an explicit spec decision (child bead). Until then the wrapper resolves and prints.
- Privacy: round one sends path names only; content excerpts go out for the finalists only.

Children: the files domain for pick; the resolving wrapper (proposal only); the execution policy decision; command-specific domains (branches, commits, processes); many-operand resolution on top of filter (hunch-bx6).
notes: 2026-09-20 planning round 2: five competing plans (lead, Opus, gpt-6-astra, gpt-5.6-sol; a Fable plan pending) blended into docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-20-jevify.md (untracked, uncommitted; the v1-to-v2 diff sits beside it). Agreed: explicit @ marker only; print only; one crate and one binary named jevify; domains are data in one record protocol {identity, handle, evidence}; the pipe is the first domain; first built-in sources are commit, branch, PR, CI run, capped at one backend window; files are not a default domain (hunch-744 stays paused). Order: filter (hunch-bx6) -> budget and quota (hunch-glz) -> held-out experiment as go/no-go -> rename and wrapper. crates.io: jevify 0.0.1 placeholder published 2026-09-20. git remote now points at tpellet/jevify.

title: pick --files: find a file by meaning, names first, content for finalists
description:
`grevi pick --files <DIR> "<description>"`: the candidates are the regular files under DIR instead of stdin lines, and the match prints as a path usable from the current directory. This is the engine of the semantic-operand epic and is useful alone: `code "$(grevi pick --files . "where man pages are parsed")"`.

Enumeration: inside a git work tree, `git ls-files -co --exclude-standard` under DIR, so .gitignore is respected with no new dependency; elsewhere a std::fs walk that does not follow symlinks. Any path with a component that starts with `.` is skipped in both modes. Paths are sorted (option order is part of the request). More than pick's MAX_LINES candidates is exit 6 with a hint to choose a narrower DIR.

Two rounds through tournament::rank, no new round: round one ranks path names only; the finals round re-ranks at most 24 finalists with `finalist_text` = path plus the first 2,000 characters of the file, redacted (the sort excerpt helper, shared, not copied). So file content of at most 24 files leaves the machine per call, and names of all candidates do.

Gate unchanged: the `any` Noul at the threshold and the winner above NONE; otherwise exit 3. `-n` works as for stdin. `--index` with `--files` is a usage error. Envelope: `data.matches[{line, text, p}]` keeps its shape with `text` = the path; `data.source` = "files".

Contract work: cli.rs help, capabilities, docs/ROBOT_MODE.md, docs/guide/verbs.md, README pick section, a PRIVACY.md row (names of all candidate files, excerpts of up to 24), the skill file. Tests: unit tests for enumeration (hidden components, symlinks, sorting, the cap) and contract tests with FakeJev (a file found by content in the finals round, abstention, usage errors, the envelope).

Gate: full quality gate. Live: a recorded spot check on this repository with 10 descriptions whose target file is fixed in advance; report hit@1, requests, latency. Numbers only from recorded runs.
notes: 2026-09-20: paused by the owner before completion; planning panel first (epic hunch-4z4). Uncommitted work in the shared checkout: src/cmd/pick.rs (--files mode, enumeration, unit tests), src/cmd/sort.rs (excerpt made pub(crate)), src/cli.rs (flag and help), src/lib.rs (dispatch), tests/pick.rs (two contract tests). State: cargo fmt and cargo check --all-targets pass; clippy, tests, ubs, docs, capabilities, PRIVACY row NOT done. Do not commit these paths until the design is settled.
close_reason: pick --files DIR delivered: names first, content for at most 24 finalists; hidden, ignored and symlinked files skipped; docs, capabilities, PRIVACY row, skill, unit and contract tests. Gate: fmt, check, clippy -D warnings, tests (all pass), ubs exit 0. Live spot check 2026-09-20, keyless backend, this repository (160 files), 10 author-written descriptions, one uncached run: 5 of 9 existing targets at top-1, 1 wrong accept (docs/guide/verbs.md for PRIVACY.md, p 0.46), 3 abstentions on existing targets (any 0.51-0.62 or 0.19, NONE won the finals), the 1 negative abstained; 3 requests and 740-1425 ms per call. title: jevify two sides: the language, fill, kinds, label
description:
Outcome: jevify speaks one language on the two sides of a command. Input side: `fill` resolves '@{kind:description}' markers to real handles and becomes the command. Output side: `why`, `pick`, `filter`, `label`, `is`; `pick`, `filter` and `label` share one byte-exact record model, `why` points and keeps its own format; `route` only prints. Kinds are coded listers or one-line recipes.

Context: docs/VISION.md decides the product. docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-21-jevify-two-sides.md decides the code and is the source of truth for every child bead; the children transcribe it. Grammar: `jevify VERB [options] ['text'…] [-- COMMAND ARGS…]`. Removed with no shim in Phase 1: `why -- CMD`, the verb name `run`, `run --yes`, `run --exec`, `run --dry-run`, `run --no-args`, the run argument pass, `pick --files DIR`, the global short flag `-v`.

Owner decisions (plan §9), final:
- No file is renamed or removed. src/cmd/run.rs keeps its name and holds `route`; src/args.rs stays on disk outside the module tree; tests/run_args.rs and tests/run_route.rs are rewritten in place.
- fill becomes the command through exec; the command's exit code comes through.
- An unsure flag abstains.
- One pool rule for every caller of `tournament::rank`: finalists per window n = 3 when 3 x windows <= W, else 2 when 2 x windows <= W, else 1; always by rank inside a window, never by a probability from another request. Capacity W x W (9,801 keyless; on TypeSafe the ceiling of 20,000 is reached first). fill uses n = 3 only, so its limit stays F = W x (W / 3). pick, pick --from and why use the full rule; why keeps MAX_KEEP = 4000.
- Per-record verbs use ask_each (the batch request of classifier.dev); independence of records is a property of the classifier backend only. meta.model stays a string, distinct models joined with ", "; fill refuses an answer when any part is not from Jev.
- `filter -v` is inversion; `--verbose` has no short flag. `--files` is a boolean on pick, filter and label. `why` is exempt from the byte-for-byte rule and takes no split option. `is` with one statement prints nothing.
- Saved inputs are content-addressed and never pruned by jevify. Only why and filter save.
- The absolute path in `source_repo_path` of the tracker export (hunch-nay) does not block this work.

Shape: each phase has a serial skeleton bead that alone writes the shared files (Cargo.toml, src/cli.rs, src/lib.rs, src/cmd/mod.rs, src/exit.rs, src/input.rs, src/output.rs), parallel beads with disjoint write sets, and contract beads (src/cmd/agent.rs, documents, skill, manifests) that wait for the behaviour they document. The version bump and `bash scripts/release.sh <full commit SHA>` belong to the release beads, which the lead does.

Division of work: workers run in a sandbox that cannot bind 127.0.0.1 or reach ~/.ssh. A worker runs fmt, check, clippy, `RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --locked --no-deps` and ubs, tries the tests and reports them as NOT RUN when the sandbox blocks them; the lead runs the full test gate, and only the lead stages, commits (signed), pushes and closes a bead. Workers never run `git add`, `git commit`, `git push` or `br close`. No language feature newer than Rust 1.87; CI runs on Linux with toolchain 1.87.0.

The tracker: workers change bead state with `br update` only and never stage .beads/. The lead exports (`br sync --flush-only`) and commits .beads/ between waves.

- Phase 1: hunch-7zg.1 (1.0), hunch-7zg.2 (1.1), hunch-7zg.3 (1.2), hunch-7zg.4 (1.3), hunch-7zg.5 (1.4), hunch-bx6 (1.5), hunch-7zg.6 (1.6), hunch-7zg.7 (1.7), hunch-sb9 (1.8 skill), hunch-7zg.8 (1.8 documents), hunch-7zg.22 (1.9 scripts and demo files); release 0.5.0 hunch-7zg.9

- Phase 3: hunch-7zg.15, hunch-7zg.16, hunch-7zg.17, hunch-7zg.18
- Phase 4: hunch-7zg.19, hunch-qxn, hunch-7zg.20; release 0.7.0 hunch-7zg.21

Outside the epic, ordered behind it: hunch-lpp (evaluation, after hunch-7zg.21), hunch-glz (quota measurement and its documentation; after hunch-7zg.3 and hunch-7zg.18), hunch-bec (after hunch-glz), hunch-4ow (demo.gif and demo.cast; after hunch-7zg.22 and hunch-glz; it does not block release 0.5.0), hunch-60l (README voice; after hunch-glz and hunch-4ow), hunch-3te (in progress elsewhere; after hunch-7zg.22). title: 1.0 Language skeleton and grammar cutover (shared files, final Outcome, route signature, -v, --files, init agents)
description:
Plan bead: 1.0 skeleton — language skeleton and grammar cutover. Epic hunch-7zg. This is the serial bead of Phase 1: it alone writes the shared files and it leaves the tree green so that 1.1–1.8 run in parallel.

Outcome: the CLI grammar is `jevify VERB [options] ['text'…] [-- COMMAND ARGS…]`. The verb `run` is `route` with its final signature, `why` takes no command, `filter` exists as a stub, `-v` belongs to `filter`, `--files` is a boolean, `init agents` parses, `Outcome` has its final shape, and the stub modules that the parallel beads fill compile.

Context: plan §1 (contract, what is removed, the three bullets under "Removed"), §2 "Changed in place", §2.3 first paragraph, §2.4 (save directory), §3 Phase 1 (the two "cutover" paragraphs), §4 (clap). Decisions, final:
- Removed with no shim: `why -- CMD`, the verb name `run`, `run --yes`, `run --exec`, `run --dry-run`, `run --no-args`, `pick --files DIR`, the global short flag `-v`. `jevify run 'x'` and `jevify why -- true` exit 2, and the one-line message gives the new form (`jevify route 'x'`; `CMD 2>&1 | jevify why`).
- `filter -v` is inversion, as `grep -v`. The global short flag `-v` of `--verbose` (src/cli.rs:36, `#[arg(short, long, global = true)]`) is removed; `--verbose` stays. tests/cli_basics.rs:52 passes `-v` for verbosity: it passes `--verbose`. Test filter inversion parsing separately from verbosity: `is 'x' -v` is exit 2; `filter -v 'x'` parses.
- `--files` is a boolean on `pick` and `filter` (and on `label` in bead 4.0): the records on stdin are paths. `pick --files DIR` (`files: Option<PathBuf>`, src/cli.rs:66-67) leaves with no shim; the form is `git ls-files | jevify pick --files 'q'` (or `fd`). The existing two-stage engine stays (path names first, excerpts for the finalists); only the source of the paths changes. To keep the tree green this bead makes src/cmd/pick.rs take the paths from its stdin lines where it walks DIR today (:27-34; `canonical_dir` :128-, `list_files` :152 and their inline tests leave with the walk, since clippy allows no dead code), and moves the `--files` tests of tests/pick.rs (:137-, :208, :230) to the stdin form with their assertions. hunch-7zg.7 completes the rewrite in place (byte records, -0, the withholding function, relative paths). `pick --index` stays as it is; `--index` with `--files` stays exit 2.
- `why` is exempt from the byte-for-byte rule: it prints each line with its number and context, as today. `Why` gets NO split option: no -0, no --para, no --files. It loses `cmd` and gains --no-save. The byte rule covers `pick`, `filter` and `label`.

Files (write set): Cargo.toml (only if needed; no new dependency), src/cli.rs, src/lib.rs, src/cmd/mod.rs, src/exit.rs, src/input.rs, src/output.rs, src/config.rs, src/records.rs (new), src/save.rs (new), src/cmd/filter.rs (new), src/cmd/why.rs, tests/why.rs, every src/cmd/*.rs for the Outcome change (add.rs, agent.rs, is.rs, pick.rs, run.rs, sort.rs), tests/cli_basics.rs, tests/run_args.rs, tests/run_route.rs, tests/pick.rs (the `--files` tests only), tests/agent.rs (only to keep it compiling and honest; its rewrite is bead 1.8). tests/live.rs is NOT in this write set: `live_run_routes_tar` is #[ignore], spawns the binary at run time and compiles unchanged; hunch-7zg.5 migrates it. Everything else is read-only. After this bead closes, the shared files are frozen for Phase 1: no other Phase 1 bead writes them, except the `pub mod args;` line in src/lib.rs (bead 1.4).

Prerequisites: hunch-ed1 (Phase 0; it writes src/config.rs, src/cmd/agent.rs and tests/agent.rs first).

Done when:
- `jevify run 'x'` and `jevify why -- true` exit 2 with a one-line message that holds the corrected form; tests/cli_basics.rs asserts both, and the --json envelope of each (error.kind, exit_code 2).
- `jevify route 'task'` dispatches to src/cmd/run.rs through `run(ctx, intent, machine)`; `RunFlags` is gone; `route --yes`, `--exec`, `--dry-run`, `--no-args` are exit 2; the seven rewritten tests pass and a sentinel proves nothing runs.
- `jevify filter 'x'` parses; `filter -v 'x'` parses; `jevify is 'x' -v` is exit 2 and `--verbose` works; `jevify is 'a' 'b' --context FILE` parses; `-0 --para` together is exit 2; `why -0`, `why --para` and `why --files` are exit 2; an argument after `--` that starts with `-` is text.
- `printf 'a.txt\nb.txt\n' | jevify pick --files 'q'` reads the paths from stdin (FakeJev) and `pick --files DIR 'q'` is exit 2; `pick --index` is unchanged.
- `jevify init agents` parses and prints a block; `init zsh` and `init bash` call `jevify route`.
- Bare `jevify` prints the quick-start card with `route` and `filter` and without `run`; tests/cli_basics.rs asserts it.
- Every `Outcome { … }` in src/ sets `exec: None`; grep finds no other value.
- A clap error for an argv that holds non-UTF-8 after `--` does not panic (args_os).
- Human output is written as bytes end to end; existing verbs print what they printed before.
- `jevify is 'a' 'b'` is an input error with no request until 1.6 (a test asserts zero requests); the refusal is in src/cmd/is.rs and the dispatch already passes `&[String]` and `Option<&Path>`.
- Dispatch passes every parsed flag: a test per verb (or a code review recorded in the finish message) shows that each flag of `Filter`, `Why`, `Pick` and `Is` reaches its `run` through the signatures above; `git grep -n "cmd::\(filter\|why\|pick\|is\)::run" src/lib.rs` shows the four calls.
- Help: an anchored grep over the output of `jevify --help` and of every `jevify VERB --help` (each verb of `VERBS`) finds none of `jevify run`, `why -- `, `-- <cmd>`, `--exec`, `--no-args`, `--files DIR`, `--files <DIR>`, `child_exit`, `jevify -v`.
- `why --no-save` parses and makes the same requests as `why` (it is excluded from the zero-request assertion).
- Zero requests for each: `pick -0 'q'` and `pick --para 'q'` ("not implemented" input error); `jevify run 'x'` has envelope `command` `jevify` and `jevify why -- true` has `command` `why`, both `error.kind` usage, exit 2.
- The moved `--files` test: five visible names plus `.env` on stdin; `.env` is a candidate by name; no captured request holds `TOKEN=1099`.
- `Exit::ALL`: no description holds "executed" or "`run`"; the test at src/exit.rs:131 passes.
- Unit tests: the terminal-check function with `true` and `false`; `save_dir(Some(..))`, `save_dir(None)` and a blank value; `read_stdin_bytes` cap and empty input; `shell_quote` over bytes: empty argument, a single quote, a non-UTF-8 byte, a newline; the save directory with and without JEVIFY_CACHE_DIR.
- The gate below passes with the whole existing suite green.

Design rules (plan §1; apply all that touch this bead):
1. Selection. Every record that pick, filter and label print is a record of the input, byte for byte. why is exempt: it points and does not reduce, so it prints each line with its number and context, as today, and takes no split option (-0, --para, --files). Every value fill substitutes is a handle that a lister printed or the caller wrote.
2. Time is the cost. A verb asks everything it can in one round, in parallel, and uses at most two rounds.
3. Asymmetric doubt. filter keeps what it is unsure about; fill and pick abstain.
4. Use the tools that exist. jevify does not do what jq, cut, grep, head, tee and cd do.
5. One role for stdin. A call never reads stdin for two purposes.

Gate, divided between the worker and the lead. Workers run in a sandbox that cannot bind 127.0.0.1 (wiremock) or reach ~/.ssh (signing).
The worker runs, from the repository root, and all must pass:
  cargo fmt --check
  cargo check --locked --all-targets
  cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings
  RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --locked --no-deps
  ubs <changed files>        # exit 0 required; verify findings, fix root causes
The worker also tries:
  cargo test --locked -- --test-threads=1
When the sandbox blocks the tests, the worker reports them as NOT RUN, with the error, never as passed. The lead then runs the full test gate outside the sandbox and sends failures back to the worker. Only the lead stages, commits (signed), pushes and closes the bead.

Rules:
- Read AGENTS.md (repository root), docs/VISION.md and the plan docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-21-jevify-two-sides.md first. The vision wins over the plan; the plan wins over this bead only where this bead is silent. Every design question of this bead is decided; nothing here waits for a decision.
- Agent Mail: register, reserve the exact write set of "Files" before the first edit (reason and thread id = this bead ID), post start and finish in that thread, release at the end. If Agent Mail is down, stop and report.
- Workers never run `git add`, `git commit`, `git push` or `br close`. The worker's last act is the finish message in the bead's thread: the files changed, the gate lines run with their results, the tests as passed or NOT RUN, scratch files left in place. The lead runs the tests, stages only the paths of "Files", commits, pushes and closes the bead.
- The tracker: a worker changes bead state with `br update` only (status, notes). Never stage, commit or edit .beads/, and never run `br sync` or `br close`. The lead exports (`br sync --flush-only`) and commits .beads/ between waves.
- One shared checkout on main. No worktree, no branch, no scratch clone, no PR. Changes of other agents in the tree are normal: never stash, revert or overwrite them.
- Never delete or rename a file. Never rm, rmdir, unlink, git rm, git stash, git restore, git reset, git clean, cargo clean, find -delete. Overwrite with an editor or write a new file. Leave scratch files in place and list them in the report. A blocked command is skipped and recorded, never routed around. Never trigger a confirmation prompt; use non-interactive flags.
- Edit code by hand, never with a script. No compatibility shim, no wrapper for a removed API, no file variants (x_v2.rs).
- For the lead's commit: only the paths of "Files" (`git commit -m "..." -- <paths>`). Subject: "<feat|fix|refactor|docs|test|chore>: <summary> (<this bead ID>)", under 72 characters. No Co-Authored-By, no session trailer. Commits are SSH-signed; never bypass signing or hooks. A new crate needs a one-line justification in the commit body; this plan adds no dependency.
- The repository is public. Before a push the lead runs: gitleaks git . --log-opts="origin/main..HEAD" --redact -v, then reads git diff origin/main..HEAD for keys, tokens, pasted API responses, absolute local paths, session URLs and personal details. On a hit, fix forward; never rewrite history, never force-push. The worker keeps all of that out of the files it writes. No communications drafts in the repository, in a bead or in a commit message.
- Never weaken, #[ignore] or delete a test to pass the gate. No live network in the default test run. Live tests (tests/live.rs) without a key are reported as NOT RUN, never as passed. Never read, print or copy a key; point jevify at it with TYPESAFE_API_KEY_FILE only.
- Rust: edition 2024, #![deny(unsafe_code)], no `set_var` in src/ (an environment a test needs is a parameter, passed through Command::env), tokio current-thread only, blocking work through spawn_blocking or std::thread::scope, argv as OsString end to end. Verify third-party APIs against docs.rs or the crate source.
- No language feature newer than Rust 1.87 (no let chains). Before the commit also run `RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --locked --no-deps`. After the lead pushes, CI runs on Linux with toolchain 1.87.0; a red CI on your commit is yours to fix forward.
- Documents state what jevify does, in the present tense, with no meta language ("this guide", "captured on") and no retrospective language ("now", "new in", "since 0.x"). History goes to CHANGELOG.md only. User-facing documents say TYPESAFE_API_KEY_FILE=/path/to/key.
- The agent-facing contract: exit codes 0 ok, 1 no, 2 usage, 3 abstain, 4 unavailable, 5 auth, 6 input, 7 child failed, 130 declined; one envelope {ok, command, version, exit_code, data, meta, error{kind, message, hint, example}}; error kinds are stable identifiers. A new verb updates cli.rs, dispatch, capabilities(), docs/ROBOT_MODE.md, README, a PRIVACY.md row and tests; in this plan the phase skeleton bead does cli.rs and dispatch, and the phase contract bead does the rest.
- A file outside "Files" is read-only. If the work needs a change there, stop, post in the thread, and let the owner of that file (named in "Files") make it.
close_reason: Grammar cutover and language skeleton. Lead gate outside the sandbox: fmt, clippy -D warnings, full cargo test --locked (17 suites pass, 4 live tests NOT RUN); worker ran check, doc and ubs exit 0. One test assertion corrected after the first gate run (request count of two why runs).

title: 2.0 fill skeleton: Fill, Pick --from, error kinds, run_cli acts on Outcome.exec, stubs
description:
Plan bead: 2.0 skeleton — fill. Epic hunch-7zg. This is the serial bead of Phase 2: it alone writes the shared files and leaves the tree green so that 2.1, 2.2 (hunch-q8p, hunch-zxz), 2.3 and 2.4 proceed.

Outcome: the CLI knows `fill` and `pick --from KIND`; the error kinds of fill exist; `run_cli` becomes a command when an outcome asks for it; the stub modules compile.

Context: plan §2 (both tables), §2.1 steps 1, 8, 9 and "New stable error kinds", §4, §9.2, §9.17. Decisions, final:
- src/cli.rs: `Fill { --dry-run, -q, --candidates FILE, --context FILE, --field N, --key NAME, -0, --para, #[arg(last = true)] cmd: Vec<OsString> }`. A command without `--` is exit 2 with the corrected example. `trailing_var_arg` stays off. After `--` every token belongs to the command, a second `--` included. `Pick` gains `--from KIND`, with clap `conflicts_with` against `--files`, `--index`, `-0` and `--para` (the fields `files`, `index`, `nul`, `para`, src/cli.rs:56-74): each combination is exit 2 from clap. A machine format on `fill` without --dry-run is exit 2. --field and --key together are exit 2.
- src/exit.rs: through the `Kinded` variant of bead 1.0 (src/exit.rs:37), the error kinds `stdin_is_tty`, `lister_failed`, `cannot_run`, `recipe_invalid` (all exit 6; `too_many` exists). A kind names only what an agent does next; the message line carries the detail. The abstention reasons of exit 3, `no_match`, `ambiguous`, `unsure_flag`, `insufficient_evidence`, are NOT `JevifyError`s and have no `error.kind`: they are `pub const … : &'static str` constants in src/exit.rs for `data.reason` and `data.markers[].reason` (an abstention is an `Outcome` with `error: null`, see hunch-bkb).
- `Outcome` does NOT change here. Bead 1.0 (hunch-7zg.1) gave it its final shape: `human: Vec<u8>` and `exec: Option<Exec>` with `struct Exec { argv: Vec<OsString>, stdin_null: bool }`, `None` at every construction site. This bead adds no field to `Outcome` and touches no src/cmd/*.rs for it; it only makes `run_cli` act on `exec`. That is why the other src/cmd/*.rs files are not in the write set and the build stays green.
- src/lib.rs: `VERBS` (:25), `command_name` (:174), dispatch, `pub mod marker; pub mod source;`; `QUICK_START` (:40-55) gains the `fill` line and its assertion in tests/cli_basics.rs follows. The dispatch arm has its final signature here: `cmd::fill::run(ctx, flags: FillFlags { dry_run, quiet, candidates, context, field, key, split }, cmd: &[OsString], machine: bool)`, where `FillFlags` is a struct of src/cmd/fill.rs (`candidates` and `context` are `Option<PathBuf>`, `field` is `Option<usize>`, `key` is `Option<String>`, `split` is the `records::Split` that the dispatch builds from `-0` and `--para` as it does for `pick`, src/lib.rs:301); hunch-bkb fills the body and never touches src/lib.rs. `run_cli` (:190) calls exec as its last act when `out.exec` is `Some`, after meta is computed and the status lines are written, and after it has flushed stdout (`std::io::stdout().flush()`; a flush error goes through `stdout_error`): `std::os::unix::process::CommandExt::exec` on `Command::new(&argv[0]).args(&argv[1..])`, with `.stdin(Stdio::null())` when `stdin_null` is true. It is a safe function, so #![deny(unsafe_code)] holds. It returns only on failure: NotFound and PermissionDenied become exit 6 `cannot_run` with the path in the message. No child, no signal forwarding, no tokio `signal` feature, no new dependency. The environment and the working directory pass through unchanged. The `debug_assert!(out.exec.is_none());` of bead 1.0 (src/lib.rs:203) is removed here.
- This bead owns the error rendering of `fill` in src/lib.rs. When the verb is `fill`, every error (clap, configuration, dispatch, a failed `exec`) is written on the human path as `jevify fill: not run: <kind>: <message>`; the hint follows as a second `jevify fill:` line unless `-q`. `report_error` (src/lib.rs:244) writes `error`, `hint` and `try` lines today (the three-line form, :245-253) and keeps them for every other verb. Machine envelopes keep their shape (:221-229 for outcomes, :255-268 for errors). On the clap path (`main_exit`, :57) the verb comes from `raw_command(&args)` (:159, called at :64), which exists, reads `args_os` and stops at `--`; no second parser is written. `-q` on that path is read from the raw arguments before `--`, as `machine_format` (:132) reads the format.
- src/output.rs: `shell_quote` exists since bead 1.0; `--dry-run` prints one command: one physical line unless an argument holds a newline, and such an argument is single-quoted with its newline kept (bash, zsh and dash read it back exactly). Add the helper that status lines use to escape a newline in a handle or an argument as `\n`, so each status line stays one line with its prefix; extend only if --dry-run needs a one-line join helper.
- The test helper is a POSIX sh script, tests/bin/argv.sh (new), run as `sh tests/bin/argv.sh <exit-code> args…`: it prints its arguments NUL-separated on stdout, prints `stdin:eof` or `stdin:data`, and exits with the given code. POSIX sh only (macOS /bin/sh and dash): no bashism. It is no Cargo target and Cargo.toml gains no `[[bin]]`, `[[test]]` or `[[example]]` entry for it: `cargo metadata` shows one bin target, jevify. Tests start it as `sh` with the script path as the first argument, so the file needs no executable bit. Non-UTF-8 arguments pass through sh unchanged; a test proves it.

Plan bead: 2.1 — marker lexer. Epic hunch-7zg.

Outcome: src/marker.rs is a pure lexer for '@{kind:description}' markers in an argv and the substitution of resolved handles. No I/O.

Context: plan §1 "Marker grammar" (all bullets), §2 file table, §2.1 steps 1 and 7, §5 first bullet, §8.2, §9.14; vision "The marker". The stub with the final signatures exists since bead 2.0 (hunch-7zg.10). Grammar, final:

  marker  := "@{" KIND ":" BODY "}"
  KIND    := "-" | [a-z][a-z-]*            the lexer keeps no registry; fill validates the name
  BODY    := bytes up to the first unescaped "}"; "\}" is a literal "}"
  one     := "@{one:" OPT ("|" OPT)* ":" QUESTION "}"      escapes \: \| \}
  flag    := "@{flag:" FLAGTEXT ":" QUESTION "}"           whole argv element; FLAGTEXT starts with "-"
  escape  := "@@{"  ->  literal "@{"

- One wrapping pair of '…' or "…" around BODY is dropped. A newline in BODY becomes a space.
- Escapes are decoded once. Substituted text is never lexed again, so a handle that holds `@{` stays literal.
- The lexer keeps NO registry and has NO unknown-kind error. `parse` knows the syntax of `-`, `one` and `flag` and returns every other syntactically valid kind as a named kind with its span (the argv index and the byte range of the marker). `fill` (hunch-bkb) validates the names against the coded kinds, the shipped recipes and, from Phase 3, the user's kinds.jsonl, before any other I/O; it owns the unknown-kind error (exit 2, the nearest kind, the `@@{` spelling) and its tests. hunch-7zg.17 extends that check to user recipes with no change to this file.
- Exit 2 from the lexer, nothing runs: `@{word:` with no closing `}`, empty BODY, BODY that is not UTF-8, `flag` embedded in a larger argument, zero markers, a `one` with fewer than two options or a repeated option, a marker in argv[0], and stdin with two roles (a `-` marker without --candidates FILE next to a `one` or `flag` marker without --context FILE).
- Every exit-2 message is one line that an agent can act on in one turn: the corrected argument in single quotes. A command given as one string (argv[0] holds a space) gets "pass the command as separate arguments".
- `@{` followed by anything that is not `KIND:` is literal (`@{u}`, `HEAD@{2}`, `@{1 day ago}`). `KIND:` is a syntactic test. The Python format string `{user}@{host:>8}` holds `@{host:`: the lexer returns it as a marker of the named kind `host` with its span. It is NOT a literal; `fill` refuses the name (exit 2, with `'{user}@@{host:>8}'`). The span lets `fill` build that corrected spelling.
- Every other byte of every argument passes through unchanged. Argv is OsString end to end (std::os::unix::ffi::OsStrExt).
- Substitution (plan §2.1 step 7): a handle is an `OsString` (`Record.handle`, src/records.rs) and is substituted as bytes, so a handle that is not UTF-8 reaches the argv unchanged. A path handle is relative to the prefix it was listed under, so 'src/@{file:…}' becomes src/cmd/add.rs; a path handle that opens its argument and starts with `-` gets `./`; a `flag` that is left out removes its whole argv element. The lexer reports, per marker: the argv index, the literal prefix and suffix, whether the marker opens its argument.
- `parse(&[OsString])` takes no list of kinds and this module holds none. The two-roles check takes the two booleans (has --candidates, has --context) as input.
- The maximum number of options of a `one` (at most W, the window of the backend) is NOT checked here: the lexer has no backend. hunch-bkb checks it in fill.

Files (write set): src/marker.rs only, with inline table tests. Everything else is read-only.

title: 2.3 pick --from KIND
description:
Plan bead: 2.3 — `pick --from KIND`. Epic hunch-7zg.

Outcome: `jevify pick --from branch 'the release automation work'` selects among a kind's candidates in place of stdin and prints the handle. It prints and runs nothing.

Context: plan §1 (pick row), §2.1 (the paragraph "One pool rule for every caller" and its table), §3 Phase 2 row 2.3 and "Done when", vision "pick --from KIND" and "A printed handle is for reading". Built on `source::enumerate` (hunch-q8p) and the tournament of hunch-zxz, both read-only here. The CLI flag exists since bead 2.0 (hunch-7zg.10). Decisions, final:
- Candidates come from `source::enumerate(kind, scope, limit, env)` with `Scope::Prefix(None)` (`enumerate` never reads stdin); with --from, stdin is not read (one role for stdin). `--from -` is refused (exit 2): stdin is the default source. `--from` with `--files`, `--index`, `-0` or `--para` is exit 2 from clap (`conflicts_with`, hunch-7zg.10). The abstention reasons `no_match` and `ambiguous` are the constants of src/exit.rs (hunch-7zg.10), in `data.reason`.
- The same decision as `fill`'s listing markers: `tournament::decide` (ratio 2, `any` threshold, NONE). `decide` serves `fill` and `pick --from` only: stdin `pick` keeps its present found rule (`any >= threshold` and best > NONE, src/cmd/pick.rs:89-94 before hunch-zxz edits that file) and its `-n N` semantics; do not change them. `decide` is `decide(&Ranking, threshold: f64)`; pass `ctx.threshold`. The signature `run(…, from: Option<&str>)` exists since bead 2.0 (hunch-7zg.10) with a "not implemented" error for `Some`; this bead fills that branch and touches no shared file.
- Rounds: `tournament::shortlist` (round 1; it returns the full `Ranking` of each window: candidates, `any`, `none`), then `source::enrich(kind, handles)` for the tier-two evidence of the finalists only (enumeration is tier one only), then `tournament::window` for the finals; no callback. The finalists come from `shortlist` in the finalist order that hunch-zxz defines (by rank, then window index: rank 1 of every window, then rank 2, then rank 3); this verb does not reorder them, and tier-two evidence goes to the first 24 of that order. With ONE window the verb decides from the `Ranking` of `shortlist` with no second request; round 2 runs only when the ratio failed and the kind has tier-two evidence.
- The kind name is validated here against the registry of src/source.rs before any other I/O: an unknown kind is exit 2 with the nearest kind and the list of kinds. With several windows, round 2 is the finals. Exit 0 found, 3 abstain (`no_match` or `ambiguous`, with the closest two on stderr), 6 `lister_failed` or `too_many`, 2 unknown kind (the message names the nearest kind and lists the kinds).
- Capacity (final, plan §2.1): `pick --from` uses the full pool rule of hunch-zxz: finalists per window n = 3 when 3 x windows <= W, else 2 when 2 x windows <= W, else 1, always by rank inside a window, never by a probability from another request; at most two rounds. Capacity is W x W candidates: 9,801 keyless; on TypeSafe the ceiling of 20,000 is reached first. The `limit` this verb passes to `enumerate` is min(W x W, 20,000). Above it: an ordered kind keeps its newest part and the status line says so (`candidates N of M, newest first`); any other kind is exit 6 `too_many` (narrow with a prefix, or pipe a narrower list into stdin `pick`). The status line says `finalists per window: N` when N is not 3. The rule lives in src/tournament.rs (read-only here); this bead passes `Finalists::Auto` and maps the capacity error.
- stdout: the handle and a newline, nothing else (the handle's bytes, unchanged). Evidence, probabilities, `candidates N, windows M` go to stderr or to the envelope. `-n N` prints the N best handles. Under a machine format a handle that is not UTF-8 is `text` (lossy), `lossy: true`, `ordinal`.
- Kinds available at this bead: `branch` (and `-` refused). Phase 3 adds the others through the registry with no change here; `route` stays on its own code until `tool` exists.

Files (write set): src/cmd/pick.rs, tests/pick.rs. Everything else is read-only.

title: Release 0.6.0 (lead only): fill
description:
Release 0.6.0, after Phase 2. Epic hunch-7zg. THE LEAD DOES THIS BEAD, not a worker: a release publishes to a public repository and to crates.io. A worker that finds this bead ready reports it to the lead and takes nothing.

Outcome: version 0.6.0 (`fill`, the marker, the kinds `-`, `branch`, `one`, `flag`, `pick --from`, the pool rule for every caller of the tournament) is tagged, built by cargo-dist and published.

Context: plan §3 (phase shape and Phase 2 "Done when"), project AGENTS.md "Release" and "Public repo: scan before every push". The contract beads do not bump the version; it happens here, last and alone. The absolute path in `source_repo_path` of .beads/issues.jsonl (hunch-nay) does not block this release.

Files (write set): Cargo.toml (version), Cargo.lock (the jevify entry), CHANGELOG.md (the 0.6.0 heading and date). Nothing else. The lead also exports the tracker (`br sync --flush-only`) and commits .beads/ between waves, in its own commit.

Prerequisites: hunch-7zg.10, hunch-7zg.23 (model provenance keeps `unknown`), hunch-7zg.11, hunch-q8p, hunch-zxz, hunch-7zg.12, hunch-bkb, hunch-7zg.13 (and through hunch-7zg.10 the release 0.5.0, hunch-7zg.9). This bead blocks hunch-7zg.15 (Phase 3) and hunch-7zg.19 (Phase 4 skeleton), so that no release carries a kind or a verb that its documents and capabilities do not name. It does not wait for the epic.

Procedure:
1. Check the Phase 2 acceptance of plan §3 by hand on the default backend (the seven commands under "Done when"); report what ran and what did not. Live tests without a key are NOT RUN.
2. Bump the version to 0.6.0 in Cargo.toml, refresh Cargo.lock (`cargo check`), set the CHANGELOG heading. Check that `cargo metadata --no-deps --format-version 1` shows one bin target, `jevify` (the test helper is the sh script tests/bin/argv.sh, no Cargo target). Run the whole gate. Commit: `chore: release 0.6.0 (hunch-7zg.14)`; no Co-Authored-By, no session trailer; signed.
3. Scan: `gitleaks git . --log-opts="origin/main..HEAD" --redact -v`, then read `git diff origin/main..HEAD`. On a hit, fix forward; never rewrite history, never force-push.
4. Push main. Wait for a successful `main` CI run on that commit. Review the outgoing release diff.
5. `bash scripts/release.sh <full commit SHA>`. Never publish the shared local working tree. Never replace an existing tag. If publishing fails, check whether the registry accepted the version before rerunning failed jobs. If only the tag push failed, inspect the retained signed tag and push that exact tag after the usual scan.

Done when: the tag v0.6.0 exists on the remote, the GitHub release has its assets, crates.io shows 0.6.0, `git status` shows main up to date with origin, and the report records the commands run.

  cargo fmt --check

  cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings
  RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --locked --no-deps
  cargo test --locked -- --test-threads=1
  ubs Cargo.toml Cargo.lock CHANGELOG.md        # every file this bead changes

That is a pass.

title: 3.1 Recipe engine, shipped recipes (src/kinds.jsonl), user kinds.jsonl
description:
Plan bead: Phase 3, first of four serial beads — the recipe engine, the shipped recipes, the user's kinds.jsonl. Epic hunch-7zg. Phase 3 is serial because every bead writes src/source.rs: this bead, then hunch-7zg.16 (coded kinds), then hunch-7zg.17 (tests and wiring), then hunch-7zg.18 (contract).

Outcome: a kind is a recipe: one JSON object on one line names the lister argv and the handle. jevify ships seven recipes as data and reads more from the user's configuration directory, never from a repository.

Context: plan §2.2 (the recipe table, the seven lines, all bullets under them, "Rules for every kind"), §5 "Recipes", §8.6; vision "A kind is a recipe". src/source.rs holds `-`, `branch`, the lister runner, the injected environment and the registry since hunch-q8p. Decisions, final:
- `#[derive(Deserialize)] #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)] struct Recipe { kind, list: Vec<String>, field: Option<usize>, key: Option<String>, ordered: bool }` (`ordered` defaults to false). With `key` the output is read as JSON lines or one array through serde_json; with `field` or neither, as lines. `field` and `key` together, an empty `list`, and a `kind` that does not match [a-z][a-z-]* are `recipe_invalid`.
- The engine is the `-` path: run `list` with the lister runner of hunch-q8p (the `try_wait` poll, `kill` on the deadline, 200 ms for the readers, the 64 MiB cap, and the validity rule: a listing counts only when the lister exited 0 and both readers reached EOF; reuse it, do not write a second one), hand the bytes to src/records.rs, get a `Listing`. The evidence of a recipe candidate is its whole record; a recipe has no evidence option and no tier two. A recipe lister receives the caller's `limit` only as the cut of the Listing (its argv is data and is not rewritten).
- Shipped recipes live in src/kinds.jsonl, compiled in with include_str!: exactly the seven lines of plan §2.2 (`pr`, `issue`, `ci-run`, `stash`, `process`, `container`, `pod`); copy them byte for byte.
- User recipes live in `kinds.jsonl` in the user's configuration directory. `Config` gains NO field in this epic: this bead adds to src/config.rs the pure function `config_dir(value: Option<&str>) -> Option<PathBuf>`, which takes the value of `JEVIFY_CONFIG_DIR` as a parameter (the variable if set and not blank, else `directories::ProjectDirs`, already a dependency), with unit tests, next to `save_dir` of bead 1.0. The production environment builder for listers lives in src/source.rs (hunch-q8p): it reads the variable once and calls `config_dir`; `source::enumerate` itself receives the directory through the injected environment (`env`). This bead also adds `"JEVIFY_CONFIG_DIR"` to the list of variables that the sanitized test command removes (`bin()`, tests/common/mod.rs:162-180), so a developer's own recipes never reach a test. hunch-7zg.18 documents the variable in docs/guide/configuration.md.
- When the file is read: only when a marker (or `pick --from`) names a kind that is neither coded nor shipped. Then EVERY line must parse: any bad line is exit 6 `recipe_invalid` with its line number, whichever kind was asked for (a line of invalid JSON names no kind, so the file is valid as a whole or not at all). For a coded or shipped kind the file is never opened, so a broken file cannot break `@{branch:…}` or `@{pr:…}`. A kind that is in no source after a clean read is the usage error "unknown kind" (exit 2, with the nearest kind) that `fill` raises (hunch-bkb owns that check, hunch-7zg.17 wires the user's file into it; the lexer keeps no registry). This bead provides the lookup in src/source.rs that both call.
- A user recipe cannot replace a coded kind or a shipped recipe: a user line named `branch` or `pr` is `recipe_invalid` with its line number (found when the file is read, under the rule above).
- jevify reads no recipe from the working directory. A cloned repository never adds a command that fill runs.
- An ordered recipe above the limit keeps its head (newest first) and says so; an unordered one is `too_many` (the caller decides; the Listing carries `ordered` and `total`).
- Lister rules: one deadline 20 s, stdin /dev/null, GH_PROMPT_DISABLED=1, GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, NO_COLOR=1; not on the PATH, not logged in or rate-limited is `lister_failed` with the tool's own text, never an empty listing.
- The registry lists every kind with its argv so that capabilities prints it (hunch-7zg.18). Listing the user's kinds for capabilities reads the file; a bad line there is reported in the capabilities data, not as a failure of `capabilities`.
- No `set_var` in src/. Inline tests pass the configuration directory, a temporary `PATH` and the deadline through the injected environment and `Command::env`. Tests that need the process environment (a user recipe through `JEVIFY_CONFIG_DIR`, a fake `gh` first on the PATH) are process-level tests in tests/fill.rs and tests/pick.rs, which belong to hunch-7zg.17.

Design rules (plan §1; apply all that touch this bead):
1. Selection. Every record that pick, filter and label print is a record of the input, byte for byte. why is exempt: it points and does not reduce, so it prints each line with its number and context, as today, and takes no split option (-0, --para, --files). Every value fill substitutes is a handle that a lister printed or the caller wrote.
2. Time is the cost. A verb asks everything it can in one round, in parallel, and uses at most two rounds.
3. Asymmetric doubt. filter keeps what it is unsure about; fill and pick abstain.
4. Use the tools that exist. jevify does not do what jq, cut, grep, head, tee and cd do.
5. One role for stdin. A call never reads stdin for two purposes.

  cargo check --locked --all-targets

Rules:
- Read AGENTS.md (repository root), docs/VISION.md and the plan docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-21-jevify-two-sides.md first. The vision wins over the plan; the plan wins over this bead only where this bead is silent. Every design question of this bead is decided; nothing here waits for a decision.
- Agent Mail: register, reserve the exact write set of "Files" before the first edit (reason and thread id = this bead ID), post start and finish in that thread, release at the end. If Agent Mail is down, stop and report.
- Workers never run `git add`, `git commit`, `git push` or `br close`. - Edit code by hand, never with a script. No compatibility shim, no wrapper for a removed API, no file variants (x_v2.rs).
- For the lead's commit: only the paths of "Files" (`git commit -m "..." -- <paths>`). Subject: "<feat|fix|refactor|docs|test|chore>: <summary> (<this bead ID>)", under 72 characters. - The repository is public. Before a push the lead runs: gitleaks git . --log-opts="origin/main..HEAD" --redact -v, then reads git diff origin/main..HEAD for keys, tokens, pasted API responses, absolute local paths, session URLs and personal details. On a hit, fix forward; never rewrite history, never force-push. The worker keeps all of that out of the files it writes. No communications drafts in the repository, in a bead or in a commit message.

The "Tier 2" of each kind below is what `enrich` returns.

The two git commands run through the lister runner of hunch-q8p, at the same time.

Tier 2: + first lines, through the one async excerpt function of src/records.rs (hunch-7zg.2; read-only), which applies the withholding function first, resolves the path against the working directory and reads inside spawn_blocking. This bead defines NO second withholding list and never calls `sort::excerpt` itself. `dir` candidates are the directories of those paths. Not ordered: above the limit is `too_many` with the two ways to narrow.
- `tool`: `inventory::load` (exists, read-only). Handle: name. Evidence: name + whatis line. - Candidates come from the working directory of the injected environment (the directory jevify runs in).
- Hidden files are listed; `.git/` never is. Excerpts are withheld by the function of src/records.rs for a path with a dot component and for `.env*`, `*.pem`, `*.key`, `id_*`, `*credentials*`, `*secret*`, `.netrc`, `.npmrc`, `.envrc`. The Listing counts them so the status line says `excerpts withheld: N`. Symlinks are not followed.
- The hygiene rules of plan §2.1 step 3 apply (newline, CR, NUL dropped and counted; a leading `-` is kept for path kinds because substitution adds `./`).
- No `set_var` and no `set_current_dir` in src/: inline tests pass the working directory, a temporary `PATH` and the deadline through the injected environment.

Files (write set): src/source.rs only, with inline tests (temporary repositories; never remove them). Everything else is read-only.

Prerequisites: hunch-7zg.15.

Done when, as inline tests:
- Tier two for finalists only: a fake `git` in the injected `PATH` records its invocations; `enumerate` of 200 commits runs `git log` and `git rev-list --count` and no per-commit command; `enrich` for 3 OIDs runs tier-two commands for those 3 only. For `file`, `enumerate` opens no listed file (a file whose content is a marker string never reaches tier-one evidence), and `enrich` reads only the given paths, withheld ones excluded and counted.

- `dir` lists directories once each.
- The prefix rule: `src/`, `--config=conf/`, and a prefix that names no directory (`lister_failed`).
- A tracked `.npmrc`, `.env.local`, `id_rsa`, `x.pem` and `a/.hidden/b.txt`: listed by path, excerpt withheld, counted; their content never appears in the evidence.
- The gate below passes.

title: 3.3 Kinds: contract tests in tests/fill.rs and fill wiring
description:
Plan bead: Phase 3, third of four serial beads — contract tests of the kinds in tests/fill.rs and tests/pick.rs, and the wiring in fill. Epic hunch-7zg.

Outcome: the kinds of hunch-7zg.15 and hunch-7zg.16 are proven end to end through `fill` and `pick --from`: prefix substitution, withheld excerpts in the status line, user recipes, lister failures, exact totals.

Context: plan §3 Phase 3 "Done when", §2.1 steps 3, 4, 7 and the status lines, §2.2, §5 "Recipes". src/cmd/fill.rs (hunch-bkb) resolves kinds through the registry of src/source.rs; this bead adds only what the new kinds need there: the prefix passed as scope for path kinds, prefix-relative substitution, tier-two evidence for `commit`, `file`, `dir` in round two, `excerpts withheld: N` and `candidates N of M, newest first` in the status lines, `recipe_invalid` surfaced with its line number. If a defect is in src/source.rs, fix it there (it is in the write set; Phase 3 is serial for that reason).
- These are the process-level tests of the design (no `set_var` in src/; inline tests of src/source.rs use an injected environment): they put fake `git`, `gh` and recipe listers first on the PATH through assert_cmd's `.env("PATH", …)`, and point at a temporary configuration directory through `.env("JEVIFY_CONFIG_DIR", …)` (the variable exists since hunch-7zg.15, and the sanitized command of tests/common/mod.rs removes it by default). `tool` (through `inventory::load`, which reads the process PATH) is tested here for the same reason.

- The user's kinds.jsonl is read only when a marker names a kind that is neither coded nor shipped; then any bad line is `recipe_invalid` with its line number, whichever kind was asked for.

Files (write set): tests/fill.rs, tests/pick.rs, src/cmd/fill.rs, src/source.rs (defect fixes only), src/cmd/pick.rs (the kind check extended to user recipes, and defect fixes; `pick --from` is tested here). src/marker.rs is read-only. Everything else is read-only (tests/common/mod.rs included).

title: 1.1 Byte records: src/records.rs
description:
Plan bead: 1.1 — byte records. Epic hunch-7zg.

Outcome: src/records.rs is the record model of `pick`, `filter`, `label` and of '@{-:…}', over raw bytes, so a record comes out exactly as it came in. It also holds the one withholding policy for file excerpts, which `--files` applies on every verb. `why` is outside this model.

Context: plan §2 (file table), §2.2 "Rules for every kind" (the withholding bullet), §2.3 "Records and the scorer" up to "The scorer", §5 "Output verbs". Bead 1.0 (hunch-7zg.1) left a compiling stub with the public signatures; fill it without changing a shared file. Decisions, final:
- `Record { handle: OsString, evidence: String, raw: Range<usize> }` indexes one input buffer. The handle is an `OsString` (byte-preserving; std::os::unix::ffi::OsStrExt / OsStringExt); `fill` substitutes it as bytes, so a path that is not UTF-8 reaches the command unchanged.
- Splitting, exactly one of: lines (default), -0 (NUL), --para (blocks between blank lines). The CLI refuses two together (exit 2, bead 1.0).
- --files is a boolean: the record is a path and the evidence is its first lines. The order is fixed: (1) the withholding function runs first; (2) the path is resolved, because `sort::excerpt` needs an absolute normalized path (src/cmd/sort.rs:46-47, read-only): join the path with the working directory, drop `.` components lexically, canonicalize the PARENT directory only, and append the final component unfollowed; a final component that is a symlink is withheld and counted; (3) the excerpt read runs inside `tokio::task::spawn_blocking`, because `excerpt` reads files and may start `pdftotext`. The module exposes one async function that takes the records to read (all of them for filter and label, the finalists for pick) and the working directory, and does the reads inside spawn_blocking; hunch-bx6, hunch-7zg.7 and hunch-qxn call it and never call `sort::excerpt` themselves. `pick --files` keeps its two stages (path names first, excerpts for the finalists only), so the function takes a subset.
- The withholding policy is ONE function here, `pub(crate)`: no excerpt for a path with a dot component, nor for `.env*`, `*.pem`, `*.key`, `id_*`, `*credentials*`, `*secret*`, `.netrc`, `.npmrc`, `.envrc`; symlinks are not followed. The path stays a record (it is listed by name); its evidence is then the path alone, and the count of withheld excerpts is returned so the verb says `excerpts withheld: N`. Phase 3's `file` kind (hunch-7zg.16) calls this function and defines no second one.
- A machine format and a record that is not UTF-8: give the verbs one helper that renders a record for the envelope as `text` (lossy UTF-8), `lossy: true` (absent or false for valid UTF-8) and the record's 1-based `ordinal` in the input, so the caller recovers the bytes from its own input or the saved input. No base64.
- JSON is jq's job: output verbs have no JSON mode. fill alone reads a handle out of a record: `--field N`, the N-th whitespace-separated field, as awk (1-based); `--key NAME`, a top-level key of a JSON value, where the input is JSON lines or one array (serde_json). The evidence is the whole record.
- Blank records are dropped. Records keep input order. CRLF, colour codes and non-UTF-8 bytes survive in `raw`. Evidence alone is decoded lossily, ANSI-stripped, clipped and redacted (`input::redact`, read-only). Byte-identical records are judged once: expose the distinct set and the map back to every occurrence.
- Input above 64 MiB is exit 6 `input_too_large`, as today. hunch-7zg.1 exclusively owns and tests the stdin size limit (`read_stdin_bytes`, src/input.rs, read-only here); this module performs no size check and has no criterion for it. `Split` (`Lines`, `Nul`, `Para`) is defined by the stub of bead 1.0 and is a parameter of `pick::run` and a field of `FilterFlags`; keep its name and variants.

Files (write set): src/records.rs only, with inline #[cfg(test)] tests. Everything else is read-only; the shared files belong to hunch-7zg.1.

Prerequisites: hunch-7zg.1.

Done when, as inline tests:
- lines, -0 and --para split correctly: empty input, one record with no terminator, trailing terminator, only blank records, CRLF line ends kept in `raw`, a block with inner single newlines under --para.
- A record with colour codes, a NUL inside a line record, and non-UTF-8 bytes: `raw` slices reproduce the input bytes exactly; the evidence is clean text.
- A non-UTF-8 handle: the whole record, `--field N` and a path under -0 each give an `OsString` whose bytes equal the input bytes.
- The envelope helper: valid UTF-8 gives `text` and `ordinal`; a non-UTF-8 record gives lossy `text`, `lossy: true` and the right 1-based `ordinal` (duplicates keep their own ordinals).
- Judge-once: duplicates map to one distinct record and come back in input order, every occurrence.
- --field: field 1, the last field, a field past the end (the record yields no handle and is counted as omitted), tabs and runs of spaces. --key: JSON lines, one array, a missing key, a non-string value (number becomes its text), invalid JSON (input error, exit 6).
- --files path resolution: `./a.txt`, `a/../b.txt`, and a directory reached through a symlinked ancestor (a macOS temporary directory is one) each give an excerpt; a final symlink is withheld and counted.
- --files: a relative path resolves against the working directory (a temporary directory passed as a parameter, not `set_current_dir`); a missing file; a directory; a non-UTF-8 path.
- Withholding: `.npmrc`, `.env.local`, `id_rsa`, `x.pem`, `a/.hidden/b.txt`, `my-credentials.json`, a symlink to a readable file: each stays a record, has no excerpt, and is counted; `src/main.rs` has an excerpt. Outcome: an answer whose model name is missing or empty is kept as the literal `unknown` from the wire to `meta.model`, so a mixed unknown/Jev answer no longer reads as Jev, and the model guard of `fill` (hunch-bkb) refuses it.

Context: plan §2.3 "The model", §2.1 step 5 "The model guard", §8.4; AGENTS.md "Incomplete evidence cannot authorize whole-input verdicts or larger actions". Bead 1.2 (hunch-7zg.3) keeps every contributing model, joined with ", " in first-seen order. The defect it left: `join_models` (src/jev/mod.rs:164-165) filters empty names out (`.filter(|s| !s.is_empty())`), during classifier parsing and during request aggregation. `Response.model` is `#[serde(default)]` (src/jev/mod.rs:88-89), so a TypeSafe response without `model` is the empty string; a classifier dimension without `model` falls back to the response's `model` (src/jev/classifier.rs:241), which may be missing too. One unknown part next to a Jev part is dropped, the joined string is `jev-…`, and `all_jev` (src/jev/mod.rs:160-161) passes. Missing provenance must not authorize an act. Decisions, final:
- The sentinel is the literal string `unknown`, one `pub const` in src/jev/mod.rs. A missing model name, an empty one and one that is only whitespace all become `unknown` at the point where the name enters: `Response` from the TypeSafe wire, and each dimension in `classifier::parse_each` / `parse_item` (src/jev/classifier.rs:204-241) after its fallback to the response's `model`.
- `join_models` keeps `unknown` like any other name: distinct, first-seen order, joined with ", ". It is kept through `classifier::parse_each`, the chunk merge of `ask_classifier` (src/jev/client.rs:415, :441), `ask_each` (the batch `Response` at :361-366 and the per-record `model:{i}` entries at :373-375 and :659-663), `Stats.model` (`record_model`, src/jev/client.rs:268-270) and the disk cache (a cached `unknown` is read back as `unknown`).
- `all_jev` is false when any part is `unknown`. It follows from the rule "every part starts with `jev`"; a unit test pins it, with `unknown` first, last and alone. The empty string stays false.
- `meta.model` stays a string and is `null`/empty only when no request was answered (`Stats.model` is `None` before the first answer); src/output.rs and src/config.rs do not change. Output verbs answer as before and name `unknown` in their status line as they name any model that is not Jev.
- The cache contract becomes `"decision_contract": 4` at both sites (src/jev/client.rs:244 and :323): an entry written under contract 3 may hold a joined model from which an empty part was dropped, so it is never read. The test `previous_cache_contract_is_bypassed_and_current_contract_hits` (tests/client.rs:78-) moves with the contract: an entry written under 3 is bypassed, one under 4 hits; the literal `"decision_contract":3` at tests/client.rs:393 becomes 4. This is the decided contract, not a weakened test.
- No new error kind, no change to the envelope, no new dependency. tests/common/mod.rs is read-only: a response without `model` is built in the test with wiremock's `ResponseTemplate` directly.

Files (write set): src/jev/mod.rs, src/jev/classifier.rs, src/jev/client.rs, tests/client.rs, tests/classifier.rs. Everything else is read-only.

Prerequisites: none. hunch-bkb (fill core) waits for this bead and holds the sentinel test "mixed unknown and Jev provenance runs nothing".

Done when, as tests:
- src/jev/mod.rs (inline): `join_models` keeps `unknown` in first-seen order and once; `all_jev("unknown")`, `all_jev("unknown, jev-fake")` and `all_jev("jev-fake, unknown")` are false; `all_jev("jev-fake, jev-next")` is true; `all_jev("")` is false; a `Response` parsed without `model`, with `"model": ""` and with `"model": "  "` has the model `unknown` (the existing `response_tolerates_missing_model_and_usage`, :239, asserts it).
- src/jev/classifier.rs (inline) and tests/classifier.rs: a dimension without `model` in a response without `model` is `unknown`; a response with one such dimension and one Jev dimension has the model `unknown, jev-…` in first-seen order, and `meta.model` of the verb's envelope carries it.

title: 1.2 Client::ask_each, parallel chunks, joined models, rate_limit_day, FakeJev vectors
description:
Plan bead: 1.2 — ask_each. Epic hunch-7zg.

Outcome: `Client::ask_each` judges up to 1,000 records per request on classifier.dev, each alone, so per-record verbs send 10 requests for 10,000 records. `ask_classifier` sends its chunks at the same time. Every contributing model is kept. A daily-quota 429 is never retried. The test fakes can express ties, batches, models and quota.

Context: plan §2.3 "The scorer" (the bullets "One request judges…", "ask_each on the wire", "The model", "429"), §5 (the FakeJev paragraph). Decisions, final:
- Signature: `Client::ask_each(records: &[String], questions: &Questions) -> impl Stream<Item = Result<(usize, Vec<Response>), JevifyError>>`; one item per batch: the batch index and one `Response` per record, in record order.
- classifier.dev: body `{"items": [r1, …, rN], "dimensions": {…}}`, the body `classifier::request_body` builds today with one item (src/jev/classifier.rs:161); `request_body` takes a slice of items. `N x questions.len() <= 1,000`. Each item keeps the 32,000-character limit (`MAX_INPUT_CHARS`, :30); a longer record is clipped as evidence is today. `classifier::parse` reads the first result only (:200-204); it becomes `parse_each`, which maps every element of `results` through the same per-dimension code and fails with a protocol error when `results.len() != N`.
- A Noul goes out as two semantic labels, as today (`noul_labels`, :45-55).
- TypeSafe: no batch form. `ask_each` sends 20 records in one state, the form of src/cmd/add.rs:10 (`BATCH`); each question names its record by id and says to judge it alone; the answers are unpacked into one `Response` per record. Independence of records is a property of the classifier backend only; do not claim it for TypeSafe in a comment, a test name or a message. `filter A | filter B = filter B | filter A` is a contract test on FakeJev (hunch-bx6), not a claim about the model.
- Redaction runs per record (`input::redact`) before the cache key is made. The cache key is per batch, as it is per request today (src/jev/client.rs:260-266), so a second run over the same input is answered from the disk.
- Batches go through `Client::post` and its semaphore.
- 429. The daily limit is HTTP 429 with a JSON body whose `code` is `rate_limit_day` (classifier.dev OpenAPI; read the error shape there and mirror it in the fake). It is never retried: exit 4 through `JevifyError::Unavailable(message)` with the message "daily quota of the free backend reached". No new variant: src/exit.rs is read-only for this bead. `rate_limit_minute` and every other 429 are retried after `Retry-After` (src/jev/client.rs:418-422). In `ask_each` a `Retry-After` up to 60 s is honoured as given, because a minute limit needs a minute; above 60 s the request is not retried: exit 4 after one request, and the message names the limit. `ask` keeps its 10 s cap (`retry_after`, src/jev/client.rs:442-451, and its test `retry_after_prefers_the_ms_header_and_caps_at_ten_seconds`, :507). The decision is one pure wait-decision function (the header value, the body's `code`, the caller) that returns wait-for or do-not-retry, so tests need no sleep. The body is already read at src/jev/client.rs:383; parse its `code` before the 429 arm (:418-422), which decides on the status alone today.
- `ask_classifier` sends its 20-question chunks one after the other today (:324-329; `MAX_DIMENSIONS`, classifier.rs:26). It sends them at the same time (`try_join_all`).
- The model. `meta.model` stays a string (src/output.rs:75 and src/config.rs:195 are `Option<String>` and stay read-only; tests/classifier.rs:63 and tests/live.rs:77 assert a string). Distinct contributing models are joined with ", " in first-seen order, and `Stats.model` holds the joined string (src/jev/client.rs:278 keeps the last one today). Every model that contributed is kept through `classifier::parse_each` (src/jev/classifier.rs:217-218 overwrites it per dimension today), through the chunk merge in `ask_classifier` (:327 `merged.model = r.model` overwrites it per chunk today) and through the disk cache (`Response.model`, src/jev/mod.rs:89, holds the joined string, so a cached answer keeps its provenance). The model guard of `fill` (hunch-bkb) requires every part to start with `jev`; expose one helper for that test (for example `Response::all_jev()` or a function in src/jev/mod.rs) so that fill and the status lines of the output verbs split the string in one place.
- The cache contract is bumped: `"decision_contract": 3` (src/jev/client.rs:261 says 2), so an entry that kept only the last model is never read.
- A 429 of `ask_each` whose `Retry-After` exceeds 60 s is not retried: exit 4, and the message names the limit from the body's `code` (`rate_limit_hour` included). Up to 60 s, `rate_limit_minute`, `rate_limit_hour` and a 429 with no readable code are retried after `Retry-After`.
- tests/common/mod.rs, test isolation: `jevify()` (:183) and `jevify_classifier()` (:192) point `JEVIFY_CACHE_DIR` at a per-test temporary directory (kept on disk, never removed), while `JEVIFY_NO_CACHE` keeps the answer cache off. The saved inputs of `why` and `filter` (hunch-bx6, hunch-7zg.7) then land in that directory and never in the developer's cache.
- FakeJev gives the winner 0.9 and spreads 0.1 (tests/common/mod.rs:26-31), so no tie and no `ambiguous` path can be written today. Add a probability vector per question, a batch responder (one result per item), a way to name the answering model per dimension, and a quota responder that returns exactly HTTP 429 with the `rate_limit_day` body (and the `rate_limit_minute` form with `Retry-After`); `FakeClassifier` is built from it. Later beads (1.5, 1.6, 2.4, label) only read tests/common/mod.rs, so deliver all of that here. (Phase 3's hunch-7zg.15 adds one line to the sanitized command, serially, after release 0.6.0.)
- Phase 0 (hunch-ed1) restricted base URLs; do not loosen it.

Everything else is read-only; the shared files belong to hunch-7zg.1. hunch-bec and hunch-glz, which also touch src/jev/client.rs, wait for this bead.

- TypeSafe backend: 45 records send three requests of 20, 20, 5; each question of a captured request names its record id.
- 0 records send no request; 1 record works; a record above MAX_INPUT_CHARS is clipped, not rejected.
- A second run over the same records sends no request (disk cache); redaction happens before the key.
- All batches of a call are in flight together up to the semaphore; `ask_classifier` with 45 questions sends its three chunks concurrently (assert with a delayed mock that the total time is near one delay, or with a barrier).
- Models: a non-Jev dimension followed by a Jev dimension in one response gives `meta.model` = "other-model, jev-fake" and the all-Jev helper says false; the same across two chunks of `ask_classifier`; the same after a cache hit; one model twice appears once. tests/classifier.rs:63 still asserts the plain string "jev-fake".
- 429: a `rate_limit_day` response is answered with exit 4 after exactly one request and the quota message; a `rate_limit_minute` response with `Retry-After: 1` is retried and succeeds; the wait-decision function, tested without sleeping: for `ask_each`, 30 s waits 30 s, 60 s waits 60 s, 61 s and 3600 s do not retry (exit 4 after one request, the message names the limit); `ask` still caps at 10 s. `git diff` shows no change in src/exit.rs.
- Cache contract: an entry written under `decision_contract: 2` for the same request is bypassed (the mock receives the request) and an entry under 3 is a hit.
- A `rate_limit_hour` 429 with `Retry-After: 3600` is not retried: exit 4 after one request, and the message names `rate_limit_hour`.
- `jevify()` and `jevify_classifier()` set `JEVIFY_CACHE_DIR` to a fresh temporary directory per command, and the existing suite writes nothing outside it.
- The fakes: a tie, a NONE close to the best, a named non-Jev model, a batch response, a `rate_limit_day` 429 and a `rate_limit_minute` 429 can each be written in one line by a test.
- The existing suite stays green with the rebuilt fakes.

title: 1.3 Saved input: src/save.rs
description:
Plan bead: 1.3 — saved input. Epic hunch-7zg.

Outcome: src/save.rs writes the full input of a reducing verb to a content-addressed file, so a reduction always leaves a way back.

Context: plan §2.4, §7, §8.5, §9.7. Bead 1.0 (hunch-7zg.1) left the stub and the save directory in src/config.rs (read-only here). Decisions, final:
- Only `why` and `filter` save. stdin `pick` saves nothing (it returns one record of a list the caller can list again) and `label` saves nothing (every record comes out). This module has two callers.
- Path: `<save dir>/outputs/<blake3-16>.log`, the name is the content hash (check Cargo.toml for the hash crate the answer cache uses; no new dependency). No slot, no index file, no lock.
- The write goes through a temporary name and a rename, as src/jev/cache.rs:42-53 does. Directory 0700, file 0600. The bytes are the raw input, secrets included.
- jevify never deletes or prunes these files.
- `<save dir>` comes from the pure function `config::save_dir(Option<&str>)` of bead 1.0 (the value of JEVIFY_CACHE_DIR, or the platform cache directory; `Config` has no field for it); it does not depend on the answer cache (--no-cache does not disable it). `--no-save` skips the save.
- The caller names the path in one summary status line, prefixed `jevify <verb>:` and written before the verb returns; it is NOT required to be the last stderr line (`--verbose` diagnostics and the error lines of `report_error` may follow it; tests assert containment, not position) (`jevify filter: kept 31 of 10074, 2 unsure, full output: PATH`; `jevify why: full output: PATH`); a failed or skipped save gives `full output: not saved (<reason>)` and `data.complete=false`. This module returns the path or the reason; it prints nothing.
- The blocking write runs through spawn_blocking at the call site; keep the API synchronous and pure of tokio. The save directory is a parameter of the API (no read of the process environment here, no `set_var` in tests).

Files (write set): src/save.rs only, with inline tests. Everything else is read-only.

Prerequisites: hunch-7zg.1.

Done when, as inline tests (temporary directories; never remove them):
