title: 1.7 Saved input in why, byte records and --files from stdin in pick
description:
Plan bead: 1.7 — saved input in `why`, byte records in `pick`. Epic hunch-7zg.

Outcome: `pick` prints the chosen record as the bytes it read, with the split modes of the record model, and `--files` reads paths from stdin; `why` saves its full input and prints the path, so its reduction leaves a way back. `why` keeps its output format.

Context: plan §1 rule 1 and the `--files` bullet, §2.3 (first part), §2.4, §3 Phase 1 row 1.7 and the paragraph "The cutover of `pick --files` spans 1.0 and 1.7", §4, §5 "Output verbs". src/records.rs (hunch-7zg.2) and src/save.rs (hunch-7zg.4) are read-only here. Bead 1.0 (hunch-7zg.1) already removed `capture` and the `cmd` argument from why.rs, made `--files` a boolean, made pick.rs take the paths from its stdin lines, and moved the `--files` tests of tests/pick.rs to the stdin form. Decisions, final:
- `why` is EXEMPT from the byte-for-byte rule: it points and does not reduce, so it prints each line with its number and context, as today (src/cmd/why.rs:197-208). `why` takes no split option (-0, --para, --files); the parser has none (bead 1.0). Do not move `why` onto src/records.rs. The byte rule covers `pick`, `filter` and `label`.
- `why` keeps `input::read_stdin` semantics for its search (lossy text is right for a log); it saves the raw bytes it read through src/save.rs before the first request, writes the one status line `jevify why: full output: PATH` before it returns (one line, prefixed `jevify why:`; it is NOT required to be the last stderr line, because `--verbose` diagnostics and the error lines of `report_error` may follow it; tests assert containment, not position), honours --no-save (a no-op since bead 1.0 until here), and sets data.complete=false with `full output: not saved (<reason>)` on a failed or skipped save. `why` needs the raw bytes and the text from one read: read bytes once (`input::read_stdin_bytes`) and decode as `read_stdin` does; never read stdin twice. `why` stays a search that returns one line with context; it does not use ask_each. Exit codes unchanged: 0 found, 3 abstain. `MAX_KEEP = 4000` (:14) stays; the pool rule that makes 4,000 kept lines resolve on the keyless backend is hunch-zxz (Phase 2), not this bead.
- `pick` reads through `input::read_stdin_bytes()` and src/records.rs: lines, -0, --para; the printed record is a slice of the input, byte for byte (colour, CRLF, non-UTF-8 survive). Twins split the Choice mass and abstain (src/cmd/pick.rs:44-46 states the rule; keep it). `pick -n 3` prints the three best. `pick --index` stays as it is (1-based numbers of stdin records; with --files it is exit 2).
- `pick --files` (boolean): the records on stdin are paths (`git ls-files | jevify pick --files 'q'`, or `fd -0 | jevify pick -0 --files 'q'`). The two-stage engine stays: round one carries path names only, round two carries excerpts for the finalists. Finalist evidence needs no callback: today `rank` selects the finalists internally and takes a synchronous `Fn(usize) -> String` (src/tournament.rs:101-144; src/cmd/pick.rs:80-82 builds it), which cannot await. `pick --files` instead calls `tournament::shortlist` (round 1; it exists, src/tournament.rs:149), fetches the excerpts of the finalists itself through the one async function of src/records.rs (the withholding function first, then the path resolved against the working directory, then the read inside spawn_blocking), then calls `tournament::window` (src/tournament.rs:55) for the finals. Until hunch-zxz (Phase 2) the finals hold the 24 best of the shortlist, as `rank` does today (:126-127; `MAX_FINALISTS` is private there, so src/cmd/pick.rs holds its own constant until then); hunch-zxz replaces that cut with the pool rule. `window` is private today: this bead makes it `pub(crate)`, the ONE change it makes in src/tournament.rs. `pick --files` always runs round two, as today (the one-window shortcut of Phase 2 is for `fill` and `pick --from` only). stdin `pick` without --files keeps `rank` and its found rule (src/cmd/pick.rs:83-88). Never call `sort::excerpt` here. A withheld path stays a candidate by name and the status line says `excerpts withheld: N`. Rewrite the `--files` tests of tests/pick.rs in place on that basis and keep what they assert (names only in round one, content only for finalists, the envelope `source`). `pick --from file` (a lister) arrives in Phase 3.
- The signatures of these verbs are `why::run(ctx, context: usize, top: usize, no_save: bool)` and `pick::run(ctx, intent: &str, top: usize, index: bool, split: Split, files: bool)`, installed and wired by bead 1.0 (hunch-7zg.1), whose dispatch passes every parsed flag; `Split` (`Lines`, `Nul`, `Para`) comes from src/records.rs. This bead fills the bodies: it may adjust a parameter type if the code demands it, never the set of parameters, and it never touches src/lib.rs or src/cli.rs.
- `pick --files` with an empty shortlist (round 1 returns no candidate, for example every window answers `NONE` with no ranked option) is exit 3 with `any: 0.0` in the envelope and NO second request.
- Any test that uses raw `cargo_bin` (not `common::jevify()` / `jevify_classifier()`) and invokes `why` or `filter` sets `JEVIFY_CACHE_DIR` to a temporary directory or passes `--no-save`.
- stdin `pick` saves nothing: it returns one record of a list the caller can list again. Only `why` and `filter` save. No --no-save on pick.
- A machine format and a record that is not UTF-8: the envelope match carries `text` (lossy), `lossy: true` and the 1-based `ordinal` (the helper of src/records.rs); no base64.
- `pick --from KIND` is bead 2.3, not this one.

Files (write set): src/cmd/why.rs, tests/why.rs, src/cmd/pick.rs, tests/pick.rs, and src/tournament.rs for exactly one change: `window` (:55) becomes `pub(crate)`. No other Phase 1 bead writes src/tournament.rs; hunch-zxz writes it in Phase 2 and keeps that visibility. Everything else is read-only. The save directory comes from `config::save_dir(Option<&str>)` (bead 1.0); `why` reads JEVIFY_CACHE_DIR and passes it.

Prerequisites: hunch-7zg.2, hunch-7zg.4 (and hunch-7zg.1 through them, which writes why.rs, pick.rs and tests/pick.rs first), and hunch-7zg.3, whose `jevify()` and `jevify_classifier()` point `JEVIFY_CACHE_DIR` at a per-test temporary directory, so the saves of these tests stay inside it.
Interim state left by bead 1.0, which this bead ends: `pick -0` and `pick --para` return a "not implemented" input error; `why --no-save` is a no-op; `pick --files` uses `visible()` (src/cmd/pick.rs:145) to give a hidden path no excerpt. This bead replaces `visible()` with the withholding function of src/records.rs (`visible()` leaves; no dead code) and keeps the assertion that no request holds `TOKEN=1099`.

Done when, as contract tests:
- pick: a coloured record, a CRLF record and a non-UTF-8 record come out byte-identical; under --json the non-UTF-8 record is `text`, `lossy: true`, `ordinal`; -0 and --para; -n 3; --index; blank input; the existing pick tests stay green, including the twin rule and MAX_LINES.
- pick --files: paths from stdin (lines and -0); a relative path; round one holds names only and round two holds excerpts of finalists only (captured requests); a `.npmrc` among the paths is a candidate by name, its content is in no request, and the status line says `excerpts withheld: 1`; `pick --files DIR` is exit 2; pick writes no file under the save directory.
- why: the output format is unchanged (the existing format tests stay green unchanged); stderr contains the one line `jevify why: full output: PATH` (containment, not position: under `--verbose` diagnostics follow it) and the file holds the exact input bytes (CRLF and non-UTF-8 included); two runs, one file; an unwritable save directory gives `not saved` and data.complete=false; --no-save; the envelope carries the path; `why -0` is exit 2.
- pick --files with an empty shortlist: exit 3, `any: 0.0`, and no request after round one (one window: exactly one request).
- pick --files with one window still sends two requests (round two always runs); `git diff` of src/tournament.rs shows the visibility of `window` and nothing else.
- No test writes outside its temporary directory: the saved inputs of `why` land under the per-test `JEVIFY_CACHE_DIR` that `jevify()` and `jevify_classifier()` set (hunch-7zg.3).
- `fill -q`-style input needs no special case: a log whose only line is `jevify fill: not run: …` can be pointed at.
- The gate below passes.

Design rules (plan §1; apply all that touch this bead):
1. Selection. Every record that pick, filter and label print is a record of the input, byte for byte. why is exempt: it points and does not reduce, so it prints each line with its number and context, as today, and takes no split option (-0, --para, --files). Every value fill substitutes is a handle that a lister printed or the caller wrote.
2. Time is the cost. A verb asks everything it can in one round, in parallel, and uses at most two rounds.
3. Asymmetric doubt. filter keeps what it is unsure about; fill and pick abstain.
4. Use the tools that exist. jevify does not do what jq, cut, grep, head, tee and cd do.
5. One role for stdin. A call never reads stdin for two purposes.

Gate, divided between the worker and the lead. Workers run in a sandbox that cannot bind 127.0.0.1 (wiremock) or reach ~/.ssh (signing).
The worker runs, from the repository root, and all must pass:
  cargo fmt --check
  cargo check --locked --all-targets
  cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings
  RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --locked --no-deps
  ubs <changed files>        # exit 0 required; verify findings, fix root causes
The worker also tries:
  cargo test --locked -- --test-threads=1
When the sandbox blocks the tests, the worker reports them as NOT RUN, with the error, never as passed. The lead then runs the full test gate outside the sandbox and sends failures back to the worker. Only the lead stages, commits (signed), pushes and closes the bead.

Rules:
- Read AGENTS.md (repository root), docs/VISION.md and the plan docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-21-jevify-two-sides.md first. The vision wins over the plan; the plan wins over this bead only where this bead is silent. Every design question of this bead is decided; nothing here waits for a decision.
- Agent Mail: register, reserve the exact write set of "Files" before the first edit (reason and thread id = this bead ID), post start and finish in that thread, release at the end. If Agent Mail is down, stop and report.
- Workers never run `git add`, `git commit`, `git push` or `br close`. The worker's last act is the finish message in the bead's thread: the files changed, the gate lines run with their results, the tests as passed or NOT RUN, scratch files left in place. The lead runs the tests, stages only the paths of "Files", commits, pushes and closes the bead.
- The tracker: a worker changes bead state with `br update` only (status, notes). Never stage, commit or edit .beads/, and never run `br sync` or `br close`. The lead exports (`br sync --flush-only`) and commits .beads/ between waves.
- One shared checkout on main. No worktree, no branch, no scratch clone, no PR. Changes of other agents in the tree are normal: never stash, revert or overwrite them.
- Never delete or rename a file. Never rm, rmdir, unlink, git rm, git stash, git restore, git reset, git clean, cargo clean, find -delete. Overwrite with an editor or write a new file. Leave scratch files in place and list them in the report. A blocked command is skipped and recorded, never routed around. Never trigger a confirmation prompt; use non-interactive flags.
- Edit code by hand, never with a script. No compatibility shim, no wrapper for a removed API, no file variants (x_v2.rs).
- For the lead's commit: only the paths of "Files" (`git commit -m "..." -- <paths>`). Subject: "<feat|fix|refactor|docs|test|chore>: <summary> (<this bead ID>)", under 72 characters. No Co-Authored-By, no session trailer. Commits are SSH-signed; never bypass signing or hooks. A new crate needs a one-line justification in the commit body; this plan adds no dependency.
- The repository is public. Before a push the lead runs: gitleaks git . --log-opts="origin/main..HEAD" --redact -v, then reads git diff origin/main..HEAD for keys, tokens, pasted API responses, absolute local paths, session URLs and personal details. On a hit, fix forward; never rewrite history, never force-push. The worker keeps all of that out of the files it writes. No communications drafts in the repository, in a bead or in a commit message.
- Never weaken, #[ignore] or delete a test to pass the gate. No live network in the default test run. Live tests (tests/live.rs) without a key are reported as NOT RUN, never as passed. Never read, print or copy a key; point jevify at it with TYPESAFE_API_KEY_FILE only.
- Rust: edition 2024, #![deny(unsafe_code)], no `set_var` in src/ (an environment a test needs is a parameter, passed through Command::env), tokio current-thread only, blocking work through spawn_blocking or std::thread::scope, argv as OsString end to end. Verify third-party APIs against docs.rs or the crate source.
- No language feature newer than Rust 1.87 (no let chains). Before the commit also run `RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --locked --no-deps`. After the lead pushes, CI runs on Linux with toolchain 1.87.0; a red CI on your commit is yours to fix forward.
- Documents state what jevify does, in the present tense, with no meta language ("this guide", "captured on") and no retrospective language ("now", "new in", "since 0.x"). History goes to CHANGELOG.md only. User-facing documents say TYPESAFE_API_KEY_FILE=/path/to/key.
- The agent-facing contract: exit codes 0 ok, 1 no, 2 usage, 3 abstain, 4 unavailable, 5 auth, 6 input, 7 child failed, 130 declined; one envelope {ok, command, version, exit_code, data, meta, error{kind, message, hint, example}}; error kinds are stable identifiers. A new verb updates cli.rs, dispatch, capabilities(), docs/ROBOT_MODE.md, README, a PRIVACY.md row and tests; in this plan the phase skeleton bead does cli.rs and dispatch, and the phase contract bead does the rest.
- A file outside "Files" is read-only. If the work needs a change there, stop, post in the thread, and let the owner of that file (named in "Files") make it.
notes: Worker implementation complete in the five reserved paths. fmt, check, clippy, rustdoc and UBS exit 0. Full and library tests blocked by sandbox EPERM creating the records non-UTF-8 fixture (80 library tests pass); pick/why wiremock tests blocked by port-bind EPERM. why -0 usage test passes. Lead must run full gate outside sandbox before closing. why uses data.saved_input and complete; zero-probability file candidates are excluded before finals so a valid NONE-only result makes no second request. No commit or close performed.
close_reason: Records and the saved input in why; byte records, split modes and stdin paths in pick; shortlist plus window for finalist excerpts. Lead gate outside the sandbox: fmt, clippy -D warnings, full cargo test --locked (18 suites pass, 4 live tests NOT RUN), ubs exit 0.

title: 1.8 Contract: 0.5.0 documents, capabilities, robot-docs, init agents
description:
Plan bead: 1.8 contract, the documents half (the skill half is hunch-sb9). Epic hunch-7zg.

Outcome: README, docs/, the repository's AGENTS.md, capabilities, robot-docs and the `jevify init agents` block teach the language of 0.5.0 in one order: the two sides (output side only), the verbs, the exit codes. The marker joins in bead 2.5.

Context: plan §6 (all), §2.4 (capabilities and PRIVACY name the save directory), §7, project AGENTS.md "Agent-facing contract". Decisions, final:
- None of the documents names a verb, a flag or a kind that the release lacks. For 0.5.0: `why`, `pick`, `filter`, `is`, `route`, `add`, `sort`, `init`, `capabilities`. `fill`, the marker, kinds, `pick --from` and `label` arrive with beads hunch-7zg.13, hunch-7zg.18 and hunch-7zg.20; write the README so that those sections slot in (the section order of plan §6 stays), without announcing them.
- README sections (plan §6 table): one sentence and the figure limited to what exists; thirty seconds (install, no key, a `filter` on a log, an `is` in an && chain); the output side: the verb table with twins, six lines of composition with jq, cut, grep, fd, head, and the way back; exit codes with "write the condition so that yes means act"; for agents; what it is not; add, sort, route; privacy, limits, license. The "Numbers" section moves to docs/guide/how-it-works.md.
- Facts the documents state (all final): `filter -v` is inversion and `--verbose` has no short flag; `--files` is a boolean on `pick` and `filter` and reads paths from stdin (`git ls-files | jevify pick --files 'q'`), and the excerpt of a hidden file or of a file that looks like a secret is withheld (`excerpts withheld: N`); `why` prints numbered lines with context and takes no split option; `is` with one statement prints nothing and with several prints `VERDICT<TAB>STATEMENT` lines; only `why` and `filter` save their input; `meta.model` is a string, several models joined with ", "; under a machine format a record that is not UTF-8 is `text`, `lossy: true`, `ordinal`; a `rate_limit_day` 429 is exit 4 "daily quota of the free backend reached" with no retry; each record is judged alone on the classifier backend only (with a key 20 records share one request).
- src/cmd/agent.rs: capabilities (verbs filter, route, is with statements and --context, why without a command; the limits: 20,000 records, 1,000 per request on classifier.dev and 20 on TypeSafe; the save directory; error kind `too_many`), robot-docs, and `init agents`: at most 25 lines, built from the capabilities table: the triggers, the verbs, the exit codes, and `jevify capabilities --json` as the source of truth. Bead 1.0 (hunch-7zg.1) added the parser value `agents` and a minimal dispatch arm; this bead writes the block. Remove every `run` execution claim (:23 and :71 name `jevify run`, :81-87 today). The `init` alias and the command_not_found hook call `jevify route` (done in bead 1.0; verify).
- AGENTS.md (repository root) belongs to this bead: the sentence on the `run` argument pass ("the documented `run` argument pass permits a third", :13-14) leaves, so the principle reads "at most two rounds of parallel Jev calls per verb"; the `why -- <cmd>` mention next to rust-version (:23-24) is restated without the removed form (1.87 stays the floor in Cargo.toml; say what needs it, or only that it is the floor); in the contract list, exit 7 "child failed" and 130 "declined": check on main which verbs still produce them (`add` and `sort` keep 130; after bead 1.4 no verb starts a child) and state exactly that.
- docs/img/: this bead owns the text around the images in the documents: README.md:39 embeds docs/img/run.svg with a caption that names `jevify run`; the caption takes the `route` form. The inner text of docs/img/run.svg (:2 and :50 show `jevify run`) is rewritten by hunch-7zg.22, which runs after this bead and before release 0.5.0. README.md:117 embeds demo.gif, a binary recording of the removed forms (`jevify -v`, `why --`, `run`): this bead REMOVES that reference (the image line; the file stays on disk), because demo.gif and demo.cast belong to hunch-4ow and do not block release 0.5.0. hunch-4ow restores the reference with the new recording.
- PRIVACY.md: a row for `filter`; the two stores: the answer cache (redacted, seven days, --no-cache) and the saved inputs (raw, never pruned, --no-save, secrets included), with the directory; the withholding list of `--files`.
- CHANGELOG.md: the 0.5.0 section, including the removals (`why -- CMD`, `run`, `--yes`, `--exec`, `--dry-run` and `--no-args` of run, the argument pass, `pick --files DIR`, the global `-v`). History lives only here.
- The version in Cargo.toml is NOT bumped here; the release bead hunch-7zg.9 does that, last and alone.
- Open bead hunch-60l (README voice rewrite) waits for hunch-7zg.18, the last contract bead; do not absorb it.

Files (write set): src/cmd/agent.rs, tests/agent.rs, src/cli.rs (help strings and `--json data:` lines only: doc comments, `after_help`, `about`; no flag, no type, no variant changes; bead 1.0 rewrote them for the 0.5.0 grammar and this bead aligns them with the final status lines and envelopes; no other open bead writes src/cli.rs while this one is open: hunch-7zg.1, .5, .6, .7 and hunch-bx6 are closed, hunch-sb9 and hunch-7zg.22 do not touch it, hunch-7zg.10 comes after release 0.5.0), AGENTS.md, README.md, docs/ROBOT_MODE.md, docs/guide/README.md, docs/guide/agents.md, docs/guide/faq.md, docs/guide/getting-started.md, docs/guide/how-it-works.md, docs/guide/verbs.md, PRIVACY.md, CHANGELOG.md. docs/guide/configuration.md only if a verb name in it is stale (hunch-ed1 wrote it). Everything else is read-only; the skill and the plugin manifests belong to hunch-sb9; demo.tape, demo-record.sh, scripts/, benchmarks/bench.sh and docs/img/run.svg belong to hunch-7zg.22.

Prerequisites: hunch-7zg.5 (route), hunch-bx6 (filter), hunch-7zg.6 (is), hunch-7zg.7 (pick and why): a contract bead waits for the behaviour it documents. Copy every status line from the binary on main, not from the plan.

Done when:
- `jevify capabilities --json` lists exactly the verbs of `VERBS`, each with usage, exit codes and data; tests/agent.rs asserts it, and asserts that `init agents` prints at most 25 lines and names no removed form.
- Anchored greps over README.md, AGENTS.md, docs/guide, docs/ROBOT_MODE.md, PRIVACY.md, src/cmd/agent.rs, the output of `jevify --help` and of every `jevify VERB --help`, and the output of `jevify capabilities --json` (it carries the descriptions of `Exit::ALL`, which bead 1.0 rewrote in src/exit.rs: no "executed", no "`run`") find none of: `jevify run`, `why -- `, `jevify fill`, `jevify label`, `@\{[a-z-]+:` (regular expression), `pick --from`, `jevify -v`. CHANGELOG.md is exempt (it names the removals). Prose such as "a paid run" or "label" as a common noun is not a hit; that is why the patterns are anchored.
- README.md holds no reference to demo.gif (`grep -n 'demo\.gif' README.md` finds only the `ffmpeg … demo.gif` example line, if it stays); demo.gif and demo.cast are untouched.
- Every example command in the documents runs against the binary from main.

- The gate below passes.

A new verb updates cli.rs, dispatch, capabilities(), docs/ROBOT_MODE.md, README, a PRIVACY.md row and tests; in this plan the phase skeleton bead does cli.rs and dispatch, and the phase contract bead does the rest.
- A file outside "Files" is read-only. If the work needs a change there, stop, post in the thread, and let the owner of that file (named in "Files") make it.
- The `ubs` gate when the changed files are only Markdown or JSON: run `ubs <changed files>`; when it reports that nothing was scanned, record "ubs: not applicable, nothing scanned" in the bead and validate every JSON file with `jq .`. That is a pass. Any file ubs does scan (Rust, shell, Python) must still exit 0.

title: Release 0.5.0 (lead only): the language, filter, is
description:
Release 0.5.0, after Phase 0 and Phase 1. Epic hunch-7zg. THE LEAD DOES THIS BEAD, not a worker: a release publishes to a public repository and to crates.io. A worker that finds this bead ready reports it to the lead and takes nothing.

Outcome: version 0.5.0 (the language: grammar cutover, byte records, `filter`, `is` with statements and --context, `route` print-only, saved input) is tagged, built by cargo-dist and published.

Context: plan §3 (phase shape: "then the version bump and the release through bash scripts/release.sh"; "A release bead runs ubs on every file it changes"), project AGENTS.md "Release" and "Public repo: scan before every push". The contract beads do not bump the version; it happens here, last and alone. The absolute path in `source_repo_path` of .beads/issues.jsonl (hunch-nay) does not block this release; the owner has said so.

Files (write set): Cargo.toml (version), Cargo.lock (the jevify entry), CHANGELOG.md (the 0.5.0 heading and date). Nothing else. The lead also exports the tracker (`br sync --flush-only`) and commits .beads/ between waves, in its own commit.

Prerequisites: hunch-ed1, hunch-7zg.1, hunch-7zg.2, hunch-7zg.3, hunch-7zg.4, hunch-7zg.5, hunch-bx6, hunch-7zg.6, hunch-7zg.7, hunch-sb9, hunch-7zg.8, hunch-7zg.22. This bead blocks hunch-7zg.10 (Phase 2 skeleton, which writes Cargo.toml next). It does not wait for the epic, and the epic does not wait for anything but its children.

Procedure:
1. Check the Phase 1 acceptance of plan §3 by hand on the default backend (the seven commands under "Done when"); report what ran and what did not. Live tests without a key are NOT RUN.
2. Bump the version to 0.5.0 in Cargo.toml, refresh Cargo.lock (`cargo check`), set the CHANGELOG heading. Run the whole gate. Commit: `chore: release 0.5.0 (hunch-7zg.9)`; no Co-Authored-By, no session trailer; signed.
3. Scan: `gitleaks git . --log-opts="origin/main..HEAD" --redact -v`, then read `git diff origin/main..HEAD`. On a hit, fix forward; never rewrite history, never force-push.
4. Push main. Wait for a successful `main` CI run on that commit. Review the outgoing release diff.
5. `bash scripts/release.sh <full commit SHA>`. The script reads the committed version and pushes its signed tag; cargo-dist builds the GitHub assets and calls publish-crates.yml. Never publish the shared local working tree. Never replace an existing tag. If publishing fails, check whether the registry accepted the version before rerunning failed jobs. If only the tag push failed, inspect the retained signed tag and push that exact tag after the usual scan.

Done when: the tag v0.5.0 exists on the remote, the GitHub release has its assets, crates.io shows 0.5.0, `git status` shows main up to date with origin, and the report records the commands run.

Gate (before the release commit, sandbox disabled):
  cargo fmt --check
  cargo check --locked --all-targets
  cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings
  RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --locked --no-deps
  cargo test --locked -- --test-threads=1
  ubs Cargo.toml Cargo.lock CHANGELOG.md        # every file this bead changes
Rules: main only, no branch, no worktree; never rm, git stash, git restore, git reset; stage and commit only these paths with `git commit -- <paths>`; never weaken a test to release. The `ubs` gate when the changed files are only Markdown, TOML or JSON: run `ubs <changed files>`; when it reports that nothing was scanned, record "ubs: not applicable, nothing scanned" in the bead and validate every JSON file with `jq .`. That is a pass. The binary recordings demo.gif and demo.cast belong to hunch-4ow and do not block this release.
close_reason: Released 0.5.0: acceptance commands ran by hand on the keyless backend (filter on test output, flow with head, jq in and out, --files, is --context, route, removed forms exit 2); full gate green; CI success on 0a507a6; scripts/release.sh pushed the signed tag v0.5.0; release workflow success; crates.io serves 0.5.0. 4 live tests NOT RUN (no key set).

title: Bound retries and subprocess work with explicit deadlines
description:
Outcome: a verb has one overall deadline with cancellation; retries wait exactly what `Retry-After` says without extra premature requests; usage in `meta` distinguishes attempts, successes, waits, cache hits and unknown usage; local `man` and `pdftotext` child processes have a timeout and bounded input.

Context: the epic hunch-7zg delivers part of the earlier scope, and this bead keeps it unchanged: hunch-7zg.3 sends classifier chunks in parallel and sets the final 429 policy (`rate_limit_day` is never retried, exit 4; other 429s are retried after `Retry-After`; one wait of `ask_each` is capped at 60 s, and a longer `Retry-After` is not retried and names the limit); hunch-q8p delivers the lister runner with its deadline (`try_wait` poll, `kill`, 200 ms for the readers, a listing valid only after exit 0 and EOF on both streams). Reuse the quota measurement of hunch-glz (benchmarks/results.md) and the telemetry evidence of hunch-hjp. Remaining scope, final:
- An overall deadline per verb, with cancellation of queued requests when it passes (exit 4 `unavailable`, the message names the deadline); the sum of retry waits never exceeds it.
- `Retry-After` behaviour: no request is sent before the named wait ends; a test proves the gap.
- Usage accounting in `meta`: attempted, succeeded, waited (count and total ms), cache hits, and unknown usage kept apart from a measured zero (`Telemetry`, src/output.rs:46; src/config.rs:190-198).
- Local child processes: `man` (src/manpage.rs, src/inventory.rs) and `pdftotext` (src/cmd/sort.rs) run with a timeout through the same poll-and-kill pattern as the lister runner (reuse it from src/source.rs if its signature allows; do not write a third one), with stdin at /dev/null and bounded output.

Files (write set): src/jev/client.rs, tests/client.rs, src/output.rs, src/config.rs (the `meta` function only; `Config` gains no field for the epic's directories, and a deadline setting, if any, is a parsed variable like the existing ones), src/manpage.rs, src/inventory.rs, src/cmd/sort.rs, tests/sort.rs, docs/ROBOT_MODE.md (the `meta` fields), docs/guide/configuration.md (the deadline variable, if one is added), CHANGELOG.md. Everything else is read-only; README.md is not in this bead.

Prerequisites: hunch-8ay (closed), hunch-7zg.3, hunch-7zg.18 (the epic's writers of these files are closed by then), hunch-glz (its measurement is reused, and it writes docs/guide/configuration.md and CHANGELOG.md first).

Done when:
- tests/client.rs: a mock that answers 429 with `Retry-After: 1` twice receives its third request no earlier than 2 s after the first; an overall deadline shorter than the waits ends with exit 4 and no further request; `rate_limit_day` behaviour is unchanged (one request, exit 4).
- `meta` under --json carries the five usage fields; a cache hit counts as a cache hit and not as a request; missing usage is null, not zero (tests/cli_basics.rs already asserts the null form and stays green).
- A fake `man` and a fake `pdftotext` that sleep are killed at the timeout and the verb continues without their text (unit tests with an injected deadline and an injected PATH through `Command::env`; no `set_var` in src/).
- docs/ROBOT_MODE.md names the `meta` fields in the present tense; CHANGELOG.md has the entry.
- The full gate passes (cargo fmt --check; cargo check --locked --all-targets; cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings; cargo test --locked -- --test-threads=1; ubs on the changed files).
- Division of the gate: the worker runs fmt, check, clippy, `RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --locked --no-deps` and ubs, and tries the tests; when its sandbox blocks them (it cannot bind 127.0.0.1) it reports them as NOT RUN with the error. The lead runs the full test gate, and only the lead stages, commits (signed), pushes and closes the bead. Workers never run `git add`, `git commit`, `git push` or `br close`. No language feature newer than Rust 1.87 (no let chains); CI runs on Linux with toolchain 1.87.0, and a red CI on this work is the worker's to fix forward. Commit subject, for the lead: "fix: <summary> (hunch-bec)", under 72 characters, no Co-Authored-By.
- The tracker: change bead state with `br update` only and never stage .beads/; the lead exports and commits it.
notes: 2026-09-21: waits for hunch-7zg.3 (epic hunch-7zg), which writes src/jev/client.rs first and delivers: classifier chunks sent in parallel, the rate_limit_day rule (HTTP 429 with body code rate_limit_day is never retried, exit 4), the 60 s cap on one wait of ask_each. The lister runner with its deadline is hunch-q8p. The remaining scope of this bead stays here: an overall deadline and cancellation for a verb, the usage accounting, the timeout of local man/pdf child processes. Reserve write paths through Agent Mail: src/manpage.rs belongs to hunch-7zg.5 and src/cmd/run.rs to hunch-7zg.5 and hunch-zxz while those are open.

title: 2.4 fill core: resolve markers and become the command
description:
Plan bead: 2.4 — fill core. Epic hunch-7zg. This bead replaces the earlier "resolving wrapper, proposal only" design: fill runs the command it resolved.

Outcome: `jevify fill -- CMD ARGS…` resolves every '@{kind:description}' marker to a real handle and becomes the command; one call replaces list, read, choose, act. Any doubt means nothing runs.

Context: plan §2.1 (all nine steps, the pool-rule table, the status lines, the error kinds), §1, §2.3 "The model", §3 Phase 2 "Done when", §5 `tests/fill.rs`, §7, §8.1–8.4, §9.2–9.5, §9.15–9.16; vision "The input side". Built on src/marker.rs (hunch-7zg.11), src/source.rs (hunch-q8p), src/tournament.rs (hunch-zxz), src/records.rs, `ask`/`ask_each` and the exec path of `run_cli` (hunch-7zg.10): all read-only here. Flow: lex -> read inputs -> enumerate -> resolve -> substitute -> print or exec. Decisions, final (owner, plan §9):
- fill becomes the command through exec: it returns `Outcome.exec = Some(Exec { argv, stdin_null })` (the field exists since bead 1.0; this bead adds nothing to `Outcome`) and `run_cli` calls `CommandExt::exec` as its last act. No child, no signal code. The command's exit code comes through; exit 7 leaves fill. `stdin_null` is true when step 2 consumed stdin, false otherwise. Everything that must reach the disk is written before exec (cache entries go through a rename; stderr is unbuffered). A literal argv[0] that is not on the PATH is exit 6 `cannot_run` before any request.
- A handle is an `OsString` (`Record.handle`) and is substituted as bytes: a handle or a path that is not UTF-8 reaches the command unchanged.
- An unsure `flag` abstains: `is::band_verdict(p, threshold, band)` (src/cmd/is.rs:121; it is `pub` and returns `(Exit, &'static str)`), called with `ctx.threshold` and the band 0.15, a constant in src/cmd/fill.rs (the default of `is --band`; `fill` has no option for it): `not run: arg 5 flag --draft: unsure 0.48; write --draft or drop the marker`. Yes keeps the argument, no removes the whole argv element.
- Windows up to F = W x (W / 3) (13,200 on TypeSafe, 3,267 on classifier.dev); fill uses three finalists per window ONLY (`Finalists::ThreeOnly` of hunch-zxz; it never goes to two or one, because a wrong act costs more than no act); the pool is never cut; at most two rounds; every request of a round is in flight at the same time. Round 1: one window per W candidates per listing marker, plus all `one` and `flag` markers over the context: one Choice per `one`, one Noul per `flag`, 20 questions per request. Round 2: one request per listing marker (finals, or the tier-two retry with one window). The `limit` fill passes to `source::enumerate` is F.
- Kind names are validated HERE, before any other I/O (no stdin read, no lister, no request): the lexer (hunch-7zg.11) keeps no registry and returns every syntactically valid kind other than `-`, `one` and `flag` as a named kind with its span. `fill` checks each name against the coded kinds and the shipped recipes of the registry in src/source.rs (from Phase 3, hunch-7zg.17 extends the same check to the user's kinds.jsonl, read only when a name is in neither, with no change to src/marker.rs). An unknown name is exit 2, nothing runs: the message names the nearest kind, lists the kinds, and shows the `@@{` spelling for a literal, built from the span: for `{user}@{host:>8}` it shows `'{user}@@{host:>8}'`.
- Rounds through the two calls of src/tournament.rs, no callback: `shortlist` (round 1; it returns the full `Ranking` of each window), then `source::enrich(kind, handles)` for the tier-two evidence of the finalists only (enumeration is tier one only; `enrich` is async, reads on the blocking pool, and runs the withholding function first for path kinds), then `window` for the finals. The finalists come from `shortlist` in the finalist order that hunch-zxz defines (by rank, then window index: rank 1 of every window, then rank 2, then rank 3); `fill` does not reorder them, and "tier-two evidence for the first 24" means the first 24 of that order. With one window, `fill` decides from the `Ranking` of `shortlist` with no second request; round 2 runs only when the ratio failed and the kind has tier-two evidence.
- `--dry-run` prints one command: one physical line unless an argument holds a newline, which stays inside its single quotes (`output::shell_quote`). Status lines on stderr escape a newline in a handle or an argument as `\n` (the helper of src/output.rs), so each status line stays one line with its prefix. Every error of `fill` is rendered by `run_cli` as `jevify fill: not run: <kind>: <message>` (hunch-7zg.10 owns that rendering).
- The leading-`-` rule lives here, per marker, because it depends on the marker's position and a listing is shared between markers (`source::enumerate` does only the unconditional hygiene: newline, carriage return, NUL): a handle that starts with `-` is dropped for a marker that opens its argument when the kind is not a path, and kept for an embedded marker. Each marker has its own omitted count in its status line and in `data.markers[]`.
- More than F candidates: an ordered kind keeps the newest F and says so; any other kind is exit 6 `too_many` with the count and the two ways to narrow (a literal path prefix, or a narrower list piped into '@{-:…}'). Zero candidates is exit 3 `no_match` with no request.
- A `one` marker holds at most W options (`Backend::window()`: 99 on classifier.dev, 200 on TypeSafe), because NONE takes one slot of the Choice; more is exit 2 with the count, before any request. The lexer has no backend, so the check lives here.
- Decision per listing marker: `tournament::decide(&Ranking, ctx.threshold)` (found when `any >= threshold` and `p(best) >= 2 x max(p(second), p(NONE))`; equal scores abstain). `one`: the same ratio over the options and NONE. Same evidence with different handles ends as `ambiguous`, and the status line says `N candidates share the same evidence`.
- The model guard: `meta.model` is a string in which distinct contributing models are joined with ", " (hunch-7zg.3). fill runs a command only when EVERY part starts with `jev`: the helper is `jev::all_jev` over `ctx.meta().model` (`pub fn all_jev(model: &str)`, src/jev/mod.rs:160 before hunch-7zg.23, which edits that file: find it by name; `Meta.model` is an `Option<String>`, src/output.rs:95, and `None` after a request was answered refuses like the empty string); do not split the string here. Otherwise the error is `JevifyError::Unavailable(format!("answered by {model}, not Jev"))`: exit 4, kind `api_unavailable` (src/exit.rs:88; no new kind), and the line names the model that is not Jev. A non-Jev dimension followed by a Jev dimension refuses. Since hunch-7zg.23 a missing or empty model name is the part `unknown`, which does not start with `jev`: a mixed unknown/Jev answer refuses too, and so does an answer with no model name at all.
- All or nothing: any abstention means nothing runs: exit 3, empty stdout, one line per failed marker: `jevify fill: not run: arg 3 branch: ambiguous; closest: tp/auth (0.41), tp/auth-v2 (0.38)`. Reasons: `no_match`, `ambiguous`, `unsure_flag`, `insufficient_evidence` (a context above the evidence budget, no request). A fill abstention is an `Outcome` (not a `JevifyError`) with exit 3 and `error: null`: `data.reason` is the reason of the FIRST failed marker in argv order, and `data.markers[]` lists every marker with its own reason (and the resolved ones with their handle). There is NO `error.kind` for an abstention: `run_cli` renders outcomes with `data` and `error: None` (src/lib.rs:221-229) and `report_error` renders errors with `error` and `data: null` (:255-268), and that code does not change. The reason strings are the constants that hunch-7zg.10 put in src/exit.rs. Errors proper (exit 2, 4, 6: usage, the model guard, `lister_failed`, `too_many`, `cannot_run`, `stdin_is_tty`) stay `JevifyError`s with `error.kind`; when a marker fails with such an error, the first one in argv order is returned.
- Enumerate each distinct (kind, prefix) once, in parallel. stdin is read once, on the blocking pool, up to 64 MiB, by `fill` itself (`source::enumerate` never reads stdin: `fill` passes the bytes in `Scope::Input { bytes, split, field, key }`); a required stdin that is a terminal is exit 6 `stdin_is_tty`. `fill` tests `std::io::stdin().is_terminal()` itself, before the read, through a pure `fn(bool) -> Result<(), JevifyError>` in src/cmd/fill.rs that returns the kind `stdin_is_tty`: `check_terminal` (src/input.rs:61) is private and returns `EmptyInput`, and src/input.rs is in no Phase 2 write set. An `EmptyInput` from the read (stdin was empty, src/input.rs:56 and :87) is not an error for `fill`: it maps to an empty listing, which becomes exit 3 `no_match` with no request. The entry point has the signature that hunch-7zg.10 fixed: `run(ctx, flags: FillFlags { dry_run, quiet, candidates, context, field, key, split }, cmd: &[OsString], machine: bool)`.
- --dry-run: the quoted command on stdout, one line, through `output::shell_quote`; exit 0. With a machine format the envelope carries data.argv; an argv that is not UTF-8 is exit 6 `cannot_run` there. A machine format without --dry-run is exit 2 (CLI, bead 2.0).
- Status lines on stderr, all prefixed `jevify fill:`, in the forms of plan §2.1; the last is `exec <quoted command>` or `not run: <reason>`. `-q` prints only `not run:` lines. jevify sets no variable for the command; environment and working directory pass through.
- Kinds at this bead: `-`, `branch`, `one`, `flag`. Phase 3 adds kinds through the registry.
- Live tests (#[ignore]) for one `branch` and one `one` per backend go into tests/live.rs (hunch-7zg.5 and hunch-bx6 wrote that file in Phase 1).

Files (write set): src/cmd/fill.rs, tests/fill.rs (new), tests/live.rs (added tests). tests/bin/argv.sh is read-only (hunch-7zg.10 owns it). Everything else is read-only.

Prerequisites: hunch-7zg.11, hunch-q8p, hunch-zxz (and hunch-7zg.10 through them), hunch-7zg.23 (model provenance keeps `unknown`; the model guard relies on it).

Done when, as contract tests in tests/fill.rs (FakeJev; the helper `sh tests/bin/argv.sh <exit-code> args…` prints its arguments NUL-separated, prints `stdin:eof` or `stdin:data`, exits with the code; PATH-dependent cases put fake `git` first on the PATH through assert_cmd's `.env`):
- The dry-run output equals the argv a run receives, a non-UTF-8 literal argument and a non-UTF-8 handle (from '@{-:…}' over -0 input) included.
- The `gh issue create` example of the vision (two `one`, one `flag`, context on stdin) sends one POST for its three markers.
- Abstain prints nothing on stdout and runs nothing; an unsure `flag` runs nothing (exit 3); an answer from another model runs nothing (exit 4), and so does a response whose first dimension is answered by another model and whose second by Jev; a sentinel file proves each. The refusal is exit 4 with `error.kind` `api_unavailable` and the message `answered by <model>, not Jev`.
- Mixed unknown and Jev provenance runs nothing: a response in which one dimension names no model and another names Jev (`meta.model` holds `unknown`) is exit 4, and the sentinel file is absent; a response with no model name at all runs nothing either.
- An unsure `flag` is decided with the band 0.15 around the threshold: with threshold 0.5, p = 0.60 and p = 0.40 abstain (`unsure_flag`), p = 0.70 keeps the argument, p = 0.30 removes the element.
- Several failed markers: a `no_match` at arg 2 and an `unsure_flag` at arg 4 give exit 3, `error` null, `data.reason` `no_match`, two `not run:` lines, and both in `data.markers[]` (under --json with --dry-run).
- Unknown kinds: `'@{widget:x}'` and `'{user}@{host:>8}'` are exit 2 before any other I/O (piped stdin is not consumed, the fake `git` records no invocation, the mock receives no request); the message names the nearest kind and holds `'{user}@@{host:>8}'`; `'{user}@@{host:>8}'` next to a real marker passes through as the literal `{user}@{host:>8}`.
- Tier two for finalists only: with several windows of branches, the fake `git` (it records its invocations) ran tier-two commands for the finalists and for no other branch; with one decisive window it ran none and the mock received one request.
- A handle that holds a newline cannot occur (enumeration drops it); a literal argument with a newline prints under --dry-run inside single quotes and reads back exactly through `sh -c`; the `exec` status line holds `\n` and stays one line.

- A lister whose child keeps the pipe open gives exit 6 `lister_failed` and sends no request (a fake `git` first on the PATH).
- A `one` with W options resolves and with W + 1 is exit 2 with the count and no request, on each backend.
- 0, 1 and 2 candidates; a tie; NONE close to the best; same evidence with different handles; a handle with a newline or a leading `-`.
- W, W + 1, F, F + 1 candidates on each backend; `F + 1` lines are `too_many` with no request; 250 lines resolve in two rounds and the finals hold three finalists of every window; fill never prints `finalists per window`; two close rivals in one window both reach the finals and end as `ambiguous`; the right candidate in the last window wins.
- A branch with a remote twin resolves.
- stdin ownership: the command prints `stdin:eof` with '@{-:…}', `stdin:data` otherwise; --candidates FILE and --context FILE leave stdin to the command; stdin with two roles is exit 2.
- The command's exit code comes through (`fill -q -- sh tests/bin/argv.sh 1 '@{-:x}' <<< x` is 1); `-q`; a machine format without --dry-run is exit 2; `one` + `flag` in one request; a `flag` no removes the element; a missing program is exit 6 `cannot_run`. "stdin is a terminal": an inline unit test of the pure function of src/cmd/fill.rs (`true` gives exit 6 with the kind `stdin_is_tty`, `false` gives `Ok`), with no process-level terminal test. An empty stdin for '@{-:…}' is exit 3 `no_match` with no request, not an input error.

- The gate below passes.

Design rules (plan §1; apply all that touch this bead):
1. Selection. Every record that pick, filter and label print is a record of the input, byte for byte. why is exempt: it points and does not reduce, so it prints each line with its number and context, as today, and takes no split option (-0, --para, --files). Every value fill substitutes is a handle that a lister printed or the caller wrote.
2. Time is the cost. A verb asks everything it can in one round, in parallel, and uses at most two rounds.
3. Asymmetric doubt. filter keeps what it is unsure about; fill and pick abstain.
4. Use the tools that exist. jevify does not do what jq, cut, grep, head, tee and cd do.

title: 1.5 filter and the scorer: print every record for which a statement is true
description:
Plan bead: 1.5 — filter and the scorer. Epic hunch-7zg.

Outcome: `CMD | jevify filter 'statement'` prints every record of its input for which the statement is true, byte for byte and in input order, keeps what it is unsure about, flows, and leaves a way back to the full input. The scorer that `label` reuses lives here.

Context: plan §1 (filter row: exit 0 kept some, 1 kept none, 3 every record unsure; the `-v` bullet), §2.3 "The scorer" (all bullets) and the `--files` and machine-format bullets above it, §2.4, §3 Phase 1 "Done when", §5 "Output verbs". - Asymmetric doubt: unsure records are kept in both directions (with and without -v). `--strict` drops the unsure. `-v` is inversion, as `grep -v`: it keeps the records where the statement is false; it is not verbosity (`--verbose` has no short flag since bead 1.0). `-c` prints the count.
- Byte-identical records are judged once; every occurrence is printed.

When the batch at the cursor arrives, its kept records are written and the cursor moves; later batches wait in the map. `run_cli` writes `Outcome.human` only after dispatch returns (src/lib.rs:151-158), which is too late for a flow: on the human path this verb writes its records straight to a locked stdout (`std::io::stdout().lock()`), handles a write error of kind BrokenPipe there as exit 0 (drop the stream, which cancels the queued requests), and returns an empty `human`. - A machine format and a record that is not UTF-8: the envelope entry carries `text` as lossy UTF-8, `lossy: true` and the record's 1-based `ordinal` (the helper of src/records.rs); no base64. The caller recovers the bytes from its own input or the saved input.

- Before the first request, on stderr: `jevify filter: 10074 records, 3120 distinct, 4 requests`. ONE summary status line, prefixed `jevify filter:` and written by the verb before it returns. The same holds for `jevify filter: answered X of Y` on a quota 429, which comes before the error lines. The line, as the vision shows: `jevify filter: kept 31 of 10074, 2 unsure, full output: PATH` (or `jevify filter: kept 31 of 10074, 2 unsure, full output: not saved (<reason>)` with data.complete=false). The input is saved before the first request unless --no-save.
- The ceiling is 20,000 distinct records: exit 6 `too_many`, no request, and the message says to narrow with grep or head. There is no flag to raise it.
- 429: a 429 whose body `code` is `rate_limit_day` is never retried by the client (hunch-7zg.3) and ends the verb with exit 4, message "daily quota of the free backend reached"; the printed records are a correct prefix and the verb writes the one status line `jevify filter: answered 3000 of 3120` before it returns the error. title: classifier.dev fallback when there is no TypeSafe key
description:
Outcome: grevi works with no TypeSafe key, by using classifier.dev as a second backend. Lead-added bead (Thomas, 2026-09-19): "have an additional bead to have classifier dev as an alternative API if you don't have a typesafe api key".

KEY FACT from Thomas (2026-09-19, supersedes any guess): classifier.dev runs Jev behind the scenes and serves it for free. So the features should be at full parity, not a degraded mode. Design for parity and prove it; do not write caveat copy about a weaker fallback unless a measurement forces you to.

What Thomas gave us: "Zero-shot text classification over plain HTTP. You send text and a list of labels, you get back the label that fits and how sure the model is. There is no API key or account required for free use... the OpenAPI 3.1 description is at https://classifier.dev/openapi.json and a short index at https://classifier.dev/llms.txt".

Step 1 - research before code (record findings in the bead notes):
- Read https://classifier.dev/llms.txt and https://classifier.dev/openapi.json (curl, sandbox disabled). Establish: endpoints, request and response shape, label limit, text size limit, rate limits, latency, whether it returns the same probabilities as Jev, and the terms of use for a client like grevi.
- Map grevi's two question kinds onto it: "which one" (choice over options plus NONE) and "is it" (absolute yes/no with a probability). Since the model is the same, the work is the wire format, not the semantics. If a shape is missing (NONE, absolute yes/no, batching, the 200-option window), say so plainly and name the workaround.
- Verify parity, do not assume it: run the existing evals (scripts/eval_run.py, scripts/eval_why.py) against both backends and record the two numbers side by side. Equal numbers are the expected result and the evidence we publish. A real gap is a finding: report it before writing any copy about it.

Step 2 - implementation (small, behind the existing client seam):
- A backend chosen by config: TypeSafe Jev when a key is present, classifier.dev when none is. GREVI_BACKEND=typesafe|classifier forces either. No key, no prompt, no signup path.
- Reuse the existing cache, retry, timeout and error mapping. Keep exit codes and the JSON envelope identical. meta reports which backend and model answered.
- health reports the active backend. capabilities lists the new env var and the backend field.
- Respect the free service: honour its rate limits, set a clear user agent (grevi/<version>), and keep concurrency conservative by default.
- Tests: contract tests with a wiremock fake for the new backend (no live network in the default run), plus one #[ignore] live test.
- Docs: README (a short "No key needed" paragraph - grevi runs out of the box, a TypeSafe key gets you your own quota), docs/guide/configuration.md and faq.md, PRIVACY.md (with this backend the text goes to classifier.dev instead of TypeSafe).

Out of scope: a local model, other providers, changing the threshold semantics, any change to the Jev path's behaviour.

Gate and rules: full gate (fmt, check, clippy -D warnings, tests, doc, cargo deny, ubs exit 0 on changed code) plus the live checks above; RULE ZERO (no rm in any form, no prompts, no redirects to variable paths); shared checkout under Agent Mail (register, reserve paths, thread = this bead ID, report to lead-0); CI pre-check, claim, work; signed commits; pre-push gitleaks and diff read; push; CI green.
notes:
Research (curl, 2026-09-19): POST https://classifier.dev/v1/classify, no key. Dimensions mode {items:[text], dimensions:{name:{labels,instructions}}} maps grevi Questions 1:1. Limits: 100 labels/dimension, 20 dimensions/request, 32,000 chars/input, 4,000 chars/instructions, 16,000 chars of definitions; free 3,000 classifications/min and 20,000/day per IP; Retry-After on 429; errors {error,code} with stable codes. PARITY CONFIRMED: a live call answers model "jev-1.13.0", the exact build grevi pins, and the 502 codes are literally typesafe_<status> - classifier.dev is a free front end to Jev, not a weaker model.
Gaps and the honest mapping: (1) 200-option window does not fit 100 labels -> the classifier backend windows at 99 + NONE; (2) per-option criteria have no field -> folded into the dimension instructions; (3) a Jev Noul is absolute, a dimension is relative -> a Noul goes out as a two-label choice between its true/false criteria (using the criteria sentences as labels, not "yes"/"no", measurably better, see below) and P(true) is that label score; (4) >20 questions -> the client splits an ask into sequential chunks of 20 and merges; (5) 32k-char input -> tournament and `is` take the min of their own budget and the backend cap; (6) usage counts classifications not tokens -> meta.input_tokens and cost_usd are 0, which is true: it is free. NONE and batching need no workaround.
Evals, both backends, GREVI_NO_CACHE=1, 2026-09-19. eval_run hand-written: 34/39 top-1 classifier vs 34/39 typesafe (abstain correct 8/10 vs 8/10). eval_run NL2Bash held-out: 34/120 vs 33/120 (abstained 70 vs 66). eval_run args spot check: tool right 9/20 vs 12/20 (n=20, grevis weakest path either way). eval_why: hit@1 14/20 and hit@3 15/20 on BOTH; data.any median 0.94 vs 0.78. Cost: $0.00 classifier, $0.53 typesafe. Verdict: parity.
First mapping attempt used plain "yes"/"no" labels for a Noul and lost 8 points on NL2Bash (26/120); switching the labels to the criteria sentences (the services own guidance: a semantic label beats a code) recovered it to 34/120. That is the change that bought parity.
Observed once in ~3,400 classifier requests: exit 4 api_protocol on one NL2Bash route (a dimension came back without scores, which the API documents as possible). Not reproducible; grevi reports it honestly as exit 4 rather than inventing a distribution.
close_reason: classifier.dev backend: keyless by default, same Jev model, parity proven on both evals. ubs exit 0 on all changed files after restructuring one match guard (self.backend == Backend::Classifier tripped its timing-safe-comparison check; now a precomputed body_rejected with matches!, behaviour identical).

title: Phase 0: JEVIFY_BASE_URL is https and host-bound; the key never follows it elsewhere
description:
Plan bead: Phase 0 — base URL. Epic hunch-7zg.

Outcome: JEVIFY_BASE_URL can no longer send the bearer token and the evidence to an arbitrary host. Today src/config.rs and src/jev/client.rs send both to whatever the variable names, and `health` builds its own client that follows redirects.

Context: plan §3 "Phase 0". Decisions, final:
- JEVIFY_BASE_URL must be https.
- The TypeSafe backend accepts only the host api.typesafe.ai; the classifier backend accepts only classifier.dev.
- 127.0.0.1 and localhost accept any scheme, for wiremock (every contract test depends on this).
- A URL with userinfo is refused.
- Redirects are not followed (reqwest redirect policy none). This also covers the `health` client built at src/cmd/agent.rs:127 (`reqwest::Client::new()`, whose default policy follows redirects): build it with the same no-redirect policy.
- Host rules: hosts are compared case-insensitively; a trailing dot is refused; an explicit port other than 443 is refused on the two known hosts.
- A refusal is a configuration error before any request; use the existing error path of src/config.rs and keep error kinds stable.
Source: src/config.rs (Backend, base URL parsing; `Backend::window` at :34; JEVIFY_CACHE_DIR at :99), src/jev/client.rs (client construction), src/cmd/agent.rs:120-135 (`health`), tests/client.rs, tests/agent.rs (the `health` tests, :63-), tests/common/mod.rs (read-only; shows how tests point jevify at wiremock).

Files (write set): src/config.rs, src/jev/client.rs, src/cmd/agent.rs (the `health` client, and the `JEVIFY_BASE_URL` string of capabilities at :38, which says "overrides the base URL of whichever backend is active" today and may state the https and host rule), tests/client.rs, tests/agent.rs (the `health` redirect test only), docs/guide/configuration.md, PRIVACY.md, CHANGELOG.md. Inline unit tests in src/config.rs. Everything else is read-only.

Prerequisites: none. This bead blocks hunch-7zg.1 (1.0), which writes src/config.rs, src/cmd/agent.rs and tests/agent.rs next.

Done when:
- tests/client.rs holds and passes: plain http refused; unknown host refused; a TypeSafe key with classifier.dev refused; userinfo refused; a 302 not followed (the mock's redirect target receives no request); localhost accepted.
- tests/agent.rs holds and passes: `jevify health` against a mock that answers 302 to a second mock never reaches the second mock (assert zero requests there), and exits with the unavailable or protocol error the existing path gives, not 0.
- Unit tests in src/config.rs, each with its expected outcome:
  - `https://API.TypeSafe.AI` (upper case) with a key: accepted, treated as api.typesafe.ai.
  - `https://api.typesafe.ai.` (trailing dot): refused.
  - `https://api.typesafe.ai:443`: accepted. `https://api.typesafe.ai:8443` and `https://classifier.dev:8443`: refused.
  - `https://api.typesafe.ai.evil.example`: refused.
  - the binding is symmetric: `https://api.typesafe.ai` for the classifier backend (no key): refused; `https://classifier.dev` with a TypeSafe key: refused.
  - `https://classifier.dev:443` for the classifier backend: accepted (an explicit 443 is accepted; any other explicit port on a known host is refused).
  - an empty or blank value: the default URL of the backend, as for every variable today (`env`, src/config.rs:73-78, treats it as unset). A value that is not a URL: refused.
  - `http://127.0.0.1:PORT` and `http://localhost:PORT`: accepted on both backends.
  - `https://user:pw@classifier.dev`: refused.
- No key or evidence reaches a refused host (assert zero requests on the mock).
- docs/guide/configuration.md and PRIVACY.md state the rule in the present tense; CHANGELOG.md has the entry.
- The gate below passes.

Design rules (plan §1; apply all that touch this bead):
1. Selection. Every record that pick, filter and label print is a record of the input, byte for byte. why is exempt: it points and does not reduce, so it prints each line with its number and context, as today, and takes no split option (-0, --para, --files). Every value fill substitutes is a handle that a lister printed or the caller wrote.
2. Time is the cost. A verb asks everything it can in one round, in parallel, and uses at most two rounds.
3. Asymmetric doubt. filter keeps what it is unsure about; fill and pick abstain.
4. Use the tools that exist. jevify does not do what jq, cut, grep, head, tee and cd do.
5. One role for stdin. A call never reads stdin for two purposes.

Gate, divided between the worker and the lead. Workers run in a sandbox that cannot bind 127.0.0.1 (wiremock) or reach ~/.ssh (signing).
The worker runs, from the repository root, and all must pass:
  cargo fmt --check
  cargo check --locked --all-targets
  cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings
  RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --locked --no-deps
  ubs <changed files>        # exit 0 required; verify findings, fix root causes
The worker also tries:
  cargo test --locked -- --test-threads=1
When the sandbox blocks the tests, the worker reports them as NOT RUN, with the error, never as passed. The lead then runs the full test gate outside the sandbox and sends failures back to the worker. Only the lead stages, commits (signed), pushes and closes the bead.

Rules:
- Read AGENTS.md (repository root), docs/VISION.md and the plan docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-21-jevify-two-sides.md first. The vision wins over the plan; the plan wins over this bead only where this bead is silent. Every design question of this bead is decided; nothing here waits for a decision.
- Agent Mail: register, reserve the exact write set of "Files" before the first edit (reason and thread id = this bead ID), post start and finish in that thread, release at the end. If Agent Mail is down, stop and report.
- Workers never run `git add`, `git commit`, `git push` or `br close`. The worker's last act is the finish message in the bead's thread: the files changed, the gate lines run with their results, the tests as passed or NOT RUN, scratch files left in place. The lead runs the tests, stages only the paths of "Files", commits, pushes and closes the bead.
- The tracker: a worker changes bead state with `br update` only (status, notes). Never stage, commit or edit .beads/, and never run `br sync` or `br close`. The lead exports (`br sync --flush-only`) and commits .beads/ between waves.
- One shared checkout on main. No worktree, no branch, no scratch clone, no PR. Changes of other agents in the tree are normal: never stash, revert or overwrite them.
- Never delete or rename a file. Never rm, rmdir, unlink, git rm, git stash, git restore, git reset, git clean, cargo clean, find -delete. Overwrite with an editor or write a new file. Leave scratch files in place and list them in the report. A blocked command is skipped and recorded, never routed around. Never trigger a confirmation prompt; use non-interactive flags.
- Edit code by hand, never with a script. No compatibility shim, no wrapper for a removed API, no file variants (x_v2.rs).
- For the lead's commit: only the paths of "Files" (`git commit -m "..." -- <paths>`). Subject: "<feat|fix|refactor|docs|test|chore>: <summary> (<this bead ID>)", under 72 characters. No Co-Authored-By, no session trailer. Commits are SSH-signed; never bypass signing or hooks. A new crate needs a one-line justification in the commit body; this plan adds no dependency.
- The repository is public. Before a push the lead runs: gitleaks git . --log-opts="origin/main..HEAD" --redact -v, then reads git diff origin/main..HEAD for keys, tokens, pasted API responses, absolute local paths, session URLs and personal details. On a hit, fix forward; never rewrite history, never force-push. The worker keeps all of that out of the files it writes. No communications drafts in the repository, in a bead or in a commit message.
- Never weaken, #[ignore] or delete a test to pass the gate. No live network in the default test run. Live tests (tests/live.rs) without a key are reported as NOT RUN, never as passed. Never read, print or copy a key; point jevify at it with TYPESAFE_API_KEY_FILE only.
- Rust: edition 2024, #![deny(unsafe_code)], no `set_var` in src/ (an environment a test needs is a parameter, passed through Command::env), tokio current-thread only, blocking work through spawn_blocking or std::thread::scope, argv as OsString end to end. Verify third-party APIs against docs.rs or the crate source.
- No language feature newer than Rust 1.87 (no let chains). Before the commit also run `RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --locked --no-deps`. After the lead pushes, CI runs on Linux with toolchain 1.87.0; a red CI on your commit is yours to fix forward.
- Documents state what jevify does, in the present tense, with no meta language ("this guide", "captured on") and no retrospective language ("now", "new in", "since 0.x"). History goes to CHANGELOG.md only. User-facing documents say TYPESAFE_API_KEY_FILE=/path/to/key.
- The agent-facing contract: exit codes 0 ok, 1 no, 2 usage, 3 abstain, 4 unavailable, 5 auth, 6 input, 7 child failed, 130 declined; one envelope {ok, command, version, exit_code, data, meta, error{kind, message, hint, example}}; error kinds are stable identifiers. A new verb updates cli.rs, dispatch, capabilities(), docs/ROBOT_MODE.md, README, a PRIVACY.md row and tests; in this plan the phase skeleton bead does cli.rs and dispatch, and the phase contract bead does the rest.
- A file outside "Files" is read-only. If the work needs a change there, stop, post in the thread, and let the owner of that file (named in "Files") make it.
close_reason: Base URL bound to the backend's HTTPS host on 443, loopback exempt, userinfo refused, redirects off for inference, prewarm and health. Lead gate outside the sandbox: fmt, clippy -D warnings, full cargo test --locked (all suites pass, 4 live tests NOT RUN), worker ran check, doc and ubs exit 0.

title: classifier.dev scores 9/20 on the run args spot check, TypeSafe 12/20
description:
Measured during hunch-classifier-fallback-41x (commit 2fd203d): the two backends tie on every eval except the 20-case argument spot check, where classifier.dev picks the right tool 9/20 against TypeSafe's 12/20. Same model (jev-1.13.0), so the gap is in the wire mapping, not the model.

Investigate before it becomes lore:
- Re-run the spot check on both backends with GREVI_NO_CACHE=1, several times, and report the spread. 20 cases is small; establish whether 9 vs 12 is real or noise.
- If real, compare the exact requests grevi sends to each backend for the same case: the man-page excerpts, the option set, the NONE handling, and how the per-option criteria are folded into instructions on classifier.dev (it has no criteria field).
- Prime suspects, in order: the 100-option cap changing the window composition; criteria folded into instructions losing per-flag definitions; the 20-questions-per-request split changing what each question sees.
- Fix the mapping if the cause is ours. If the free service genuinely cannot express what the args pass needs, document that one line honestly in README and docs/guide/configuration.md rather than hiding it.

Also in scope, cheap: one transient api_protocol (exit 4) fired in about 3,400 classifier requests when a dimension came back with no scores (documented as nullable). Not reproducible. Decide whether one retry on that shape is right, or whether reporting it honestly is already correct.

Gate: full gate plus the live eval runs, with the numbers in the close reason.

title: Keyless backend: measure the daily quota per verb and document it
description:
Outcome: the documents and `capabilities` state, from a recorded measurement, what the free keyless backend (classifier.dev) allows in a day: how many classifications each verb costs, and so how many `jevify route`, `filter`, `pick`, `why` and `is` calls fit the daily quota from one IP.

Context: observed 2026-09-19 on classifier.dev without a key, from one IP: after roughly twenty routing calls over a PATH of about 2,200 commands (plus a few hundred `is`, `pick`, `why` calls), every request returned HTTP 429; an agent that looped `is` over 24 files stalled past its 120 s timeout. Hypothesis, not verified: routing scores every command on the PATH, so one call costs about as many classifications as there are commands, and nine calls reach the documented 20,000 per day per IP. The routing verb is `jevify route` since hunch-7zg.1 (it only prints); the concurrency variable is `JEVIFY_CONCURRENCY`.
The 429 policy is final and is NOT part of this bead; hunch-7zg.3 delivers it and this bead keeps it unchanged: HTTP 429 with body `code` `rate_limit_day` is never retried, exit 4, message "daily quota of the free backend reached"; `rate_limit_minute` and every other 429 are retried after `Retry-After`; one wait of `ask_each` is capped at 60 s, and a 429 whose `Retry-After` exceeds the cap is not retried and names the limit (`rate_limit_hour` included). This bead changes no retry code and does not touch src/jev/client.rs.
Scope, final: quota measurement and its documentation. A cheaper first pass for `route` on the classifier backend (a local prefilter, BM25 then Jev) is NOT in this bead; if the measurement shows it is needed, file it as a new bead with the routing evals as its gate.

Files (write set): README.md (the quota text only: "No key needed" and "Limits"), docs/guide/configuration.md (the rate-limit row of the backend table and the free-calls line), docs/guide/faq.md (the quota answer), src/cmd/agent.rs (`capabilities.backends`: the quota fields only) with tests/agent.rs, benchmarks/results.md (one appended, dated measurement section), CHANGELOG.md. Everything else is read-only. README quota text belongs to this bead; hunch-60l rewrites the README's voice only after it, and hunch-bec reuses this measurement.

Prerequisites: hunch-7zg.3 (the final 429 policy), hunch-7zg.18 (the last contract bead of the epic hunch-7zg; the contract beads own README.md and src/cmd/agent.rs until then). hunch-bec and hunch-60l wait for this bead.

Done when:
- A dated measurement in benchmarks/results.md gives, per verb (`route` over a stated PATH size, `pick` and `why` over stated line counts, `filter` and `label` over stated record counts, `is`), the classifications counted by jevify (`meta`) against the service's own accounting where the service reports it, with the binary version, the backend, the date and `JEVIFY_CONCURRENCY`. The measurement stops before it exhausts the shared daily quota; what could not be measured is reported as NOT RUN.
- README "Limits" and docs/guide/configuration.md state the real number of free calls per day per verb as a range with its conditions, next to the measurement date; `capabilities.backends` carries the same figures and tests/agent.rs asserts the fields exist.
- The documented 429 behaviour matches hunch-7zg.3 word for word (no fail-fast rule of its own, no `GREVI_*` name, no `jevify run`).
- Present tense, no meta, no retrospective language outside CHANGELOG.md; dates only next to the measurement.
- The full gate passes (cargo fmt --check; cargo check --locked --all-targets; cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings; cargo test --locked -- --test-threads=1; ubs on the changed files, and when ubs reports that nothing was scanned for Markdown or JSON, record "ubs: not applicable, nothing scanned").
- Division of the gate: the worker runs fmt, check, clippy, `RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --locked --no-deps` and ubs, and tries the tests; when its sandbox blocks them (it cannot bind 127.0.0.1) it reports them as NOT RUN with the error. The lead runs the full test gate, and only the lead stages, commits (signed), pushes and closes the bead. Workers never run `git add`, `git commit`, `git push` or `br close`. No language feature newer than Rust 1.87 (no let chains); CI runs on Linux with toolchain 1.87.0, and a red CI on this work is the worker's to fix forward. Commit subject, for the lead: "docs: <summary> (hunch-glz)", under 72 characters, no Co-Authored-By.
- The tracker: change bead state with `br update` only and never stage .beads/; the lead exports and commits it.
notes:
During hunch-q3i scoped live audit, classifier probes repeatedly returned api_unavailable after about 30 seconds with meta.requests=0. This confirms observed unavailability and counter underreporting, not quota as the cause. Stop probes rather than consume more shared quota; report semantic/boundary checks unavailable. See E2E_AUDIT.md and telemetry bead hunch-hjp.

title: Decide the execution policy for user-written commands with resolved operands
description:
Owner decision needed. The governing plan (docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-18-hunch-v0.md, Constraints and decisions; Task R3) keeps unvalidated command grammar a proposal, and `run` executes only zero-argument true, false, pwd, ls, even with --yes. The semantic-operand wrapper wants to execute a user-written command after grevi substituted a handle.

Argument for a separate, wider policy: in `run` the model chooses the tool and the flags; in the wrapper the user wrote both and the model only chose among existing handles of a declared domain. The residual risk is a wrong handle inside a command with a large effect (rm, mv, kill, git reset), chosen on path-name and excerpt evidence, which R4 calls incomplete evidence for a whole-file action.

Proposed policy to accept, amend or reject: (1) the never-execute list applies to the head command and the proposal is printed only; (2) on a terminal the resolved command and p are shown and the default answer is no; `--yes` skips the question; (3) machine mode needs `--exec --yes`, the child's stdout goes to stderr, child failure is exit 7; (4) no execution when any handle sits within 0.06 of the threshold (the measured jitter); (5) the spec and AGENTS.md principles state the user-written-grammar distinction in one sentence. If accepted: fixtures first (wrong-handle, leading-dash name, declined, never-execute head, no TTY), then the code.
notes: Decided per docs/VISION.md (hunch-vq2): fill prints by default and --run executes. jevify keeps no effect classes, action floors or escalating-flag tables; the caller's permission system decides what may run. Abstention (exit 3) and the margin check are the only guards jevify owns.
close_reason: Superseded by docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-21-jevify-two-sides.md (epic hunch-7zg), section 9.2: the owner decided that fill becomes the command through exec and that the caller's permission system decides what may run.

title: Post-release: update the local install and evaluate jevify on real agent tasks
description:
Outcome: After the 0.7.0 release is published, the local jevify install is updated to it, and jevify is evaluated on real agent tasks: how agents pick it up next to other CLI tools, and how `fill`, `is`, `filter`, `why`, `pick`, `label` and the kinds behave in practice. Done by the lead, not a worker. This bead is no child of the epic hunch-7zg: the epic closes when its children close, and this bead starts after the release bead hunch-7zg.21.
Context: Owner request of 2026-09-21. Plan section "After the language is stable"; every item of that section is an acceptance criterion below. Use Jev itself as a judge for extra feedback: `jevify is` and `jevify label` over agent transcripts (for example "the agent used fill where a listing was needed", "the agent read a long output that filter or why would have reduced"). Agents under test get only the skill or the `jevify init agents` block, never hints in the task. The older evaluation beads (hunch-ric, hunch-3te, hunch-s18, hunch-evl) target the endpoint set of 0.4.0; reuse their task families and gold where a verb survives (`pick`, `why`, `is`, `route`), and file what is missing for the new verbs as new beads here.
Files: no repository source file. Findings go into new beads (one per defect) and into a report outside the repository or under evals/ if the owner asks.
Prerequisites: hunch-7zg.21 (the 0.7.0 release bead).
Done when:
- `jevify --version` on this machine prints the released version.
- A local invocation log exists: every jevify call of the evaluation with its verb, flags, exit code, record and request counts, elapsed time and model, kept on this machine (never in the repository), and the report is computed from it.
- A held-out set per verb and per kind exists (`fill` per kind `-`, `branch`, `commit`, `file`, `dir`, `tool`, one recipe kind, `one`, `flag`; `pick`, `pick --from`, `why`, `filter`, `label`, `is`, `route`), labelled by someone other than the author of the verb, and the report gives the result per set.
- Recall of `filter` at the unsure boundary is measured: over the held-out set, how many true records fall in the unsure band, how many are lost under `--strict`, and the recall with and without it.
- How often the right candidate misses the finalists of its window is measured, for n = 3, 2 and 1 finalists per window (the pool rule of plan §2.1), on lists above one window.
- A set of real agent tasks (git, gh, cargo, logs, files, kubectl/docker if present) has run with and without jevify available; per task: did the agent reach for jevify, which verb, exit codes, turns and tokens saved or lost, wrong picks, misquoted markers, abstentions.
- Jev as a judge: `jevify is` and `jevify label` labels over the transcripts, with the statements used, and a spot check of those labels by hand.
- A short report with the defects filed as beads. Live runs that could not happen are reported as NOT RUN.
