title: 2.2 Kinds - and branch: src/source.rs, the lister runner, the registry
description:
Plan bead: 2.2, the source half — the kinds `-` and `branch` in src/source.rs (the pool-rule half of 2.2 is hunch-zxz, which writes src/tournament.rs). Epic hunch-7zg. This bead replaces the earlier "operand domains" design; commits, files, dirs, tools and recipes are Phase 3 (hunch-7zg.15, hunch-7zg.16), which continue this file after Phase 2.

Outcome: `source::enumerate(kind, scope, limit, env) -> Listing { records, total, omitted, ordered }` lists candidates with their evidence for `-` (the bytes of stdin or --candidates FILE, which the caller read and passes in `scope`) and `branch`, under one deadline, never through a shell, with an injected environment.

Context: plan §2 file table, §2.1 step 3, §2.2 (the coded-kinds table rows `-` and `branch`, the bullets "The lister runner", "The environment is injected", "Listers take a limit", "Rules for every kind"), §5, §8.7. The stub with the final signatures and the kind registry exists since bead 2.0 (hunch-7zg.10). Decisions, final:
- `scope` is an enum, with the shape the stub of hunch-7zg.10 fixed: `enum Scope { Input { bytes, split, field, key }, Prefix(Option<PathBuf>) }`. `Input` serves the kind `-`: the CALLER reads stdin or --candidates FILE (once, on the blocking pool) and passes the bytes with `split: records::Split`, `field: Option<usize>` and `key: Option<&str>`; `enumerate` NEVER reads stdin. `Prefix` serves path kinds (the literal prefix of the marker, Phase 3); `branch` takes `Prefix(None)`. A scope that does not fit the kind is an internal usage error.
- `-`: records through src/records.rs (read-only): `records::parse` (:21), then `records::field` (:88) for --field N or `records::key` (:111) for --key; reuse them, write no second parser. Handle (an `OsString`): by --key / --field N / the whole record; evidence is the whole record; `raw` is the record's range in the given bytes; no tier two.
- `branch`: lister `git for-each-ref --sort=-committerdate --format=… refs/heads refs/remotes`. Handle: the local short name; `origin/x` for a remote-only ref. Tier 1: name, tip subject, age computed by code. Tier 2: + last 5 subjects, changed top-level paths: the distinct top-level paths of the branch's last 5 commits (`git log -5 --name-only <ref>`). A branch record indexes no input buffer, so its `raw` is `0..0`. One candidate per branch: a remote ref whose local branch exists is folded into it, and symbolic refs (origin/HEAD) are skipped. `branch` is an ordered kind (newest first).
- The limit: listers take a `limit` from the caller (F for fill, the capacity of plan §2.1 for `pick --from`). An ordered kind above the limit keeps its newest `limit` and the Listing carries `total`, so the status line `candidates N of M, newest first` is exact. The caller decides `too_many` for an unordered kind; the Listing carries `ordered` and `total`.
- The lister runner: `std::process::Command` with piped stdout and stderr, two detached reader threads that send bytes over a channel (std::sync::mpsc), and a `try_wait` poll every 20 ms until the deadline. On the deadline: `kill`, `wait`, then at most 200 ms for the readers, then return `lister_failed`. A LISTING IS VALID ONLY WHEN THE LISTER EXITED 0 AND BOTH READER THREADS REACHED EOF. If the readers have not finished 200 ms after the exit, or after a kill, the result is `lister_failed`: a descendant that still holds the pipe cannot block jevify, and a partial listing never reaches Jev or `fill` (incomplete evidence cannot authorize an act, AGENTS.md). The grace pattern in words: after the child has exited (or was killed), the readers get a short fixed time to reach EOF, and jevify stops waiting for them after it; a lister feeds a run, so what was read by then is discarded, never used. Output above 64 MiB stops the read and is `lister_failed`. No process group, no new rustix feature, no new dependency. `tokio::time::timeout` around a blocking task is NOT the mechanism: a started blocking task cannot be aborted. The runner itself runs inside spawn_blocking so the runtime keeps driving HTTP. One deadline: 20 s. stdin /dev/null, GH_PROMPT_DISABLED=1, GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, NO_COLOR=1. A failure, a missing tool: exit 6 `lister_failed` with a bounded tail of the tool's stderr, never an empty listing. Build this runner so the recipe engine (hunch-7zg.15) reuses it.
- The production builder of the environment lives here, in src/source.rs: it reads the process environment once (`PATH`, the working directory, the 20 s deadline; from Phase 3 the configuration directory through `config::config_dir`). `Config` gains no field in this epic and src/config.rs is read-only here.
- The environment is injected: `enumerate` and the runner take `PATH`, the configuration directory and the deadline as parameters (`env`), and the runner passes `PATH` through `Command::env`. No `set_var` in src/ (#![deny(unsafe_code)]; edition 2024 marks it unsafe). Inline tests pass a temporary `PATH` and a short deadline through that parameter. Cases that depend on the process environment are process-level tests in tests/fill.rs (hunch-bkb) and tests/pick.rs (hunch-7zg.12) through assert_cmd's `.env`.
- Candidate hygiene (plan §2.1 step 3): enumeration does only the unconditional part: a handle that holds a newline, a carriage return or a NUL is dropped and counted in `omitted`. The leading-`-` rule depends on the marker's position and a listing is shared between markers, so it is NOT here: hunch-bkb applies it per marker. A handle that starts with `-` stays in the Listing. Two candidates with the same handle and evidence are one. Same evidence with different handles stay separate. `total` is the count before any cut.
- Candidates come from the directory jevify runs in (the working directory is a field of `env` too, so tests need no `set_current_dir`). jevify never reads the scope out of the tool's flags.
- Enumeration is TIER ONE ONLY: `enumerate` for `branch` runs the one `for-each-ref` command and no per-branch command. Tier-two evidence comes from `enrich(kind, handles) -> Vec<String>` (async; the git reads go through the lister runner on the blocking pool; for path kinds the withholding function of src/records.rs runs first), which returns tier-two evidence for the given finalists only, in the order of `handles`. This bead delivers `enrich` for `branch` (the last 5 subjects and the changed top-level paths of each given branch) and returns an empty evidence for `-`; hunch-7zg.16 extends it for `commit`, `file`, `dir`. hunch-bkb and hunch-7zg.12 call it after `tournament::shortlist`.
- The registry of kinds (name, coded or recipe, ordered, path kind, has tier two) lives here; src/cmd/fill.rs and src/cmd/pick.rs read it to validate a kind name. src/marker.rs keeps no registry and does not read it.

Files (write set): src/source.rs only, with inline tests (temporary git repositories built by the test; a fake `git` script in a temporary directory passed as the injected `PATH` for the failure paths). Contract tests of these kinds are in tests/fill.rs (hunch-bkb) and tests/pick.rs (hunch-7zg.12). Everything else is read-only.

Prerequisites: hunch-7zg.10.

Done when, as inline tests:
- `-` through `Scope::Input` (the test passes bytes; nothing reads stdin): whole record, --field, --key over JSON lines and one array; duplicates folded; a handle with a newline, a carriage return or a NUL dropped and counted; a handle with a leading `-` kept; a non-UTF-8 handle kept byte for byte; empty input gives an empty listing (the caller turns it into `no_match`).
- `branch`: a local branch with a remote twin is one candidate with the local name; a remote-only ref is `origin/x`; origin/HEAD is skipped; the age text comes from code; order is newest first; tier two holds the last 5 subjects and the top-level paths changed in those 5 commits (a path changed only in the sixth commit is absent); every branch record has `raw == 0..0`; with `limit` 3 and 5 branches the Listing holds the newest 3 and `total` 5; outside a git repository is `lister_failed` with git's text.
- `enrich`: a fake `git` in the injected `PATH` records its invocations; `enumerate` of 50 branches runs one git command; `enrich` for 3 handles runs tier-two commands for those 3 only, and no tier-two command runs for a non-finalist; the result keeps the order of `handles`.
- The runner, with an injected short deadline: a lister that prints more than a pipe buffer on both streams does not block; a lister that sleeps past the deadline is killed and gives `lister_failed` within the deadline plus 200 ms plus a margin; a lister that prints some lines and exits 0 at once while its background child keeps the pipe open and sleeps returns within the grace time (it does not wait for the child) and is `lister_failed`: the lines it printed are not returned as a Listing, so no request can follow; a lister that exits 1 after printing lines is `lister_failed`; an output above the cap (inject a small cap for the test) is `lister_failed`; a missing program; the environment variables are set; stdin is /dev/null.
- grep finds no `set_var` and no `set_current_dir` in src/source.rs.
- The gate below passes.

Design rules (plan §1; apply all that touch this bead):
1. Selection. Every record that pick, filter and label print is a record of the input, byte for byte. why is exempt: it points and does not reduce, so it prints each line with its number and context, as today, and takes no split option (-0, --para, --files). Every value fill substitutes is a handle that a lister printed or the caller wrote.
2. Time is the cost. A verb asks everything it can in one round, in parallel, and uses at most two rounds.
3. Asymmetric doubt. filter keeps what it is unsure about; fill and pick abstain.
4. Use the tools that exist. jevify does not do what jq, cut, grep, head, tee and cd do.
5. One role for stdin. A call never reads stdin for two purposes.

Gate, divided between the worker and the lead. Workers run in a sandbox that cannot bind 127.0.0.1 (wiremock) or reach ~/.ssh (signing).
The worker runs, from the repository root, and all must pass:
  cargo fmt --check
  cargo check --locked --all-targets
  cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings
  RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --locked --no-deps

title: 4.1 label: tag each stdin record with one of the caller's labels
description:
Plan bead: Phase 4 — `label`. Epic hunch-7zg.

Outcome: `CMD | jevify label a,b,c` prints each record of its input with one of the caller's labels, as `LABEL<TAB>RECORD`, so `cut`, `sort` and `uniq -c` make a histogram by meaning.

Context: plan §3 Phase 4, §2.3 "The scorer" (ask_each, flow, the model, 429, the ceiling) and the `--files` and machine-format bullets, §5 "Output verbs"; vision "a tag on each record". Built on src/records.rs (hunch-7zg.2), `Client::ask_each` (hunch-7zg.3) and the scorer that src/cmd/filter.rs exposes as pub(crate) (hunch-bx6): all read-only. The CLI and the stub exist since hunch-7zg.19. Decisions, final:
- One Choice per record, the labels plus an internal `NONE`, through `ask_each`: 1,000 records per request on classifier.dev (N x questions <= 1,000), 20 on TypeSafe (one state, each question names its record). Independence of records is a property of the classifier backend only. Byte-identical records are judged once.
- At most W labels (`Backend::window()`: 99 on classifier.dev, 200 on TypeSafe), because NONE takes one slot of the Choice: more is exit 2 with the count, before any request. The parser has no backend, so the check lives here, after `Config::load`.
- Output is `LABEL<TAB>RECORD`, the record byte for byte, in input order; with -0 the terminator is NUL. An unsure record has the label `?`: unsure means NONE wins, or the best label fails the ratio `p(best) >= 2 x max(p(second), p(NONE))` (the constant of src/tournament.rs, read-only).
- The way back, stated exactly: for line records, `cut -f2-` of the output equals the input WITHOUT ITS BLANK LINES (blank records are dropped by src/records.rs). With -0 and --para the label prefixes the first line of the record, and the claim there is "the record follows the tab unchanged" (a paragraph that holds a tab on a later line is not recovered by `cut`; the bytes after the first tab of the output record are the record).
- A machine format and a record that is not UTF-8: the envelope entry carries `text` (lossy), `lossy: true` and the 1-based `ordinal` (the helper of src/records.rs), next to the label; no base64.
- `--files`: the records are paths, the evidence is the excerpt through the one async function of src/records.rs (withholding first, the working directory, spawn_blocking); `excerpts withheld: N` in the status line.
- Exit 0 labelled, 3 every record unsure. Probabilities go to stderr or the envelope, never to stdout.
- Flow (records written straight to a locked stdout on the human path, an empty `human` returned, BrokenPipe is exit 0), the counts line before the first request (`jevify label: N records, D distinct, R requests`), the ceiling of 20,000 distinct records (exit 6 `too_many`), the `rate_limit_day` prefix (exit 4, `answered X of Y`, no retry) and the model line behave exactly as in filter; reuse the scorer, do not copy it.
- `label` does not save its input: every record comes out, so nothing is reduced. Only `why` and `filter` save.
- No --ordered, no Score wire type, no --report, no several label sets (cut on purpose, plan "Later").

Files (write set): src/cmd/label.rs, tests/label.rs (new). Everything else is read-only; if the scorer in src/cmd/filter.rs lacks a hook, post in this thread and let the lead assign the change.

Prerequisites: hunch-7zg.19, hunch-7zg.3, hunch-7zg.2, hunch-bx6.

Done when, as contract tests (exit code and --json envelope for each path):
- `label bug,feature,question | cut -f1 | sort | uniq -c` gives a histogram.
- Line records: `cut -f2-` of the output equals the input without its blank lines; the test input holds a blank line, a record with a tab, colour codes, CRLF and non-UTF-8 bytes.
- --para: a paragraph that holds a tab on its second line: the bytes after the first tab of the output record equal the paragraph. -0: the same with NUL terminators.
- Under --json a non-UTF-8 record is `text`, `lossy: true`, `ordinal`, with its label.
- W labels resolve and W + 1 are exit 2 with the count and no request, on each backend.
- An unsure record is `?`; every record unsure is exit 3; a tie is `?`; NONE wins is `?`.
- 2,500 records on the classifier backend send three requests; 20,001 distinct records send none; duplicates are judged once and all printed.
- Flow and a closed stdout (exit 0); the `rate_limit_day` prefix; a non-Jev model named in the status line; empty stdin; --files with a `.npmrc` (withheld, counted, absent from the request); label writes no file under the save directory.

Design rules (plan §1; apply all that touch this bead):
1. Selection. Every record that pick, filter and label print is a record of the input, byte for byte. why is exempt: it points and does not reduce, so it prints each line with its number and context, as today, and takes no split option (-0, --para, --files). Every value fill substitutes is a handle that a lister printed or the caller wrote.
2. Time is the cost. A verb asks everything it can in one round, in parallel, and uses at most two rounds.
3. Asymmetric doubt. filter keeps what it is unsure about; fill and pick abstain.
4. Use the tools that exist. jevify does not do what jq, cut, grep, head, tee and cd do.
5. One role for stdin. A call never reads stdin for two purposes.

title: Rust best practices: tooling, tests, clean CI/CD
description:
Outcome: hunch follows current Rust tooling, testing and CI/CD best practice, so CI is clean, reproducible and easy to extend with GitHub Actions: a pinned toolchain file, an MSRV check, locked builds, rustdoc and dependency-audit checks, cached and least-privilege workflows, dependency update automation and complete Cargo metadata. Lead-added bead (Thomas, 2026-09-19): "verify that we follow Rust best practices when it comes to tooling/testing etc. so that we have clean CI/CD and can easily integrate with GitHub Actions if needed." Not in the original plan; this bead is its spec.

Read first: ~/.claude/AGENTS.md and /Users/tpellet/Projects/hunch/AGENTS.md (every time); Cargo.toml, .github/workflows/ci.yml, .gitignore, .gitleaks.toml, the plan's "## Global Constraints" and Task 16 (cargo-dist owns the release workflow, which Task 16 generates AFTER this bead: do not create release.yml here). Verify every third-party action, tool and config key against its current primary docs before use (GitHub docs, the action's README, docs.rs, the cargo book); record the URLs you checked in the close reason.

Context:
- Before claiming: run the CI pre-check (the "Before claiming" step of the CI criterion in Done when); only then claim: `br update <this-id> --claim --actor worker-<short-id> --json`.
- Audit first, then change. Write a short checklist in the bead notes (`br update --append-notes`): each item below as PASS (already true, with evidence) / FIXED (what changed) / SKIPPED (why). Do not churn what is already right.
- Checklist:
  1. Toolchain: add `rust-toolchain.toml` pinning the same toolchain CI uses (1.93.1, components rustfmt and clippy) so local and CI match; CI keeps `dtolnay/rust-toolchain` at the same version.
  2. MSRV: a CI job (ubuntu only) that runs `cargo check --locked --all-targets` on the declared `rust-version` (1.87) so the floor is real; if it fails, report it — do not raise `rust-version` silently; fixing the MSRV is a finding for the lead.
  3. Locked, reproducible builds: `Cargo.lock` committed (it is a binary); CI uses `--locked` on check/clippy/test; `cargo fmt --all --check`.
  4. Tests: `cargo test --locked --all-targets -- --test-threads=1` plus `cargo test --locked --doc`; live tests stay `#[ignore]` and never run in CI (no secrets in CI); no network in default tests.
  5. Docs: `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --locked --no-deps` passes (fix broken intra-doc links in place if any).
  6. Supply chain: add `cargo-deny` with a minimal `deny.toml` (advisories, licenses allow-list covering the current dependency tree as MIT-compatible for this MIT project, bans duplicates as warn, sources crates.io only) and a CI job using the official `EmbarkStudios/cargo-deny-action`; run `cargo deny check` locally first (install with `cargo install cargo-deny --locked`, outside the sandbox). A real advisory is a finding: fix by `cargo update -p <crate>` if a patched version exists, else record and report.
  7. Workflow hygiene: `permissions: contents: read` at the top; `concurrency` group with `cancel-in-progress: true` for PR/branch runs; `Swatinem/rust-cache` for build caching; `actions/checkout` on its current major (the Node 20 deprecation annotation seen on CI run 35445297521 must disappear); job `timeout-minutes`; matrix stays ubuntu-latest + macos-latest. Validate with `actionlint` (`brew install actionlint`, outside the sandbox) — exit 0.
  8. Dependency automation: `.github/dependabot.yml` for `cargo` and `github-actions`, weekly, grouped minor/patch.
  9. Cargo metadata: `description`, `license = "MIT"`, `repository`, `homepage` (repo URL), `readme`, `keywords` (≤5), `categories` (valid crates.io slugs, e.g. command-line-utilities), `rust-version`; keep `publish = false` (crates.io name taken) and the cargo-dist `dist = true` rule for Task 16 intact. Optional `[profile.release]` `lto = "thin"`, `codegen-units = 1`, `strip = true` ONLY with a measured before/after of binary size and `hunch --version` wall time (AGENTS.md: no performance claim without a baseline); otherwise SKIPPED.
  10. Lints: a `[lints.rust]` table with `unsafe_code = "forbid"` is equivalent to the crate attribute; add it only if it does not conflict with the tests' permitted `unsafe { set_var }` (tests/ are separate crates — check); otherwise SKIPPED with the reason.
  11. README: a CI status badge at the top, linking to the ci.yml workflow (one line; keep Thomas's voice rules from 13b/13d for any prose).
- Never weaken a gate: no `continue-on-error`, no dropped platforms, no `#[ignore]`/deleted tests, no clippy allows to get green.
- Files: Create: rust-toolchain.toml, deny.toml, .github/dependabot.yml. Modify: .github/workflows/ci.yml, Cargo.toml, README.md (badge only), and source files only to fix rustdoc -D warnings findings. Do not touch src logic, the plan's verified code or release.yml.
- AFK RULE: never run any command that needs a human confirmation or that dcg blocks (rm, rm -rf, git reset --hard, git clean, git stash, git checkout -- <path>, force-push, mv over an existing file, redirects to variable paths); skip, record with --append-notes, continue.

Done when:
- [ ] Checklist items 1–11 recorded in notes as PASS / FIXED / SKIPPED with evidence.
- [ ] Local gate with the sandbox disabled: `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo check --locked --all-targets`, `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --locked -- --test-threads=1`, `cargo test --locked --doc`, `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --locked --no-deps`, `cargo deny check`, `actionlint` — all exit 0. `ubs` on changed code files exit 0, or "ubs: not applicable — nothing scanned (exit 3)" when only non-code changed; never an override.
- [ ] One signed commit `chore: harden CI and Rust tooling (<this-id>)` staging exactly the files above plus `.beads/issues.jsonl` (claim and close ride in it; `br close` then `br sync --flush-only` before committing). No Co-Authored-By, no Claude-Session trailer.
- [ ] Pre-push scan: `gitleaks git . --log-opts="origin/main..HEAD" --redact -v` no leaks, and read `git diff origin/main..HEAD` for keys, tokens, absolute local paths in user-facing files, emails, session URLs, personal details; on a hit fix forward, never rewrite history. Global rule: ~/.claude/AGENTS.md "Public Repositories — Push With Care".
- [ ] CI (outside the sandbox): Before claiming, `gh run list --workflow ci.yml --branch main --limit 3 --json databaseId,headSha,status,conclusion` and match `headSha` to `git rev-parse origin/main`; wait for it; a red run belongs to the bead whose push turned it red. After your push, match your `HEAD` SHA, `gh run watch <databaseId>`, and every job (including the new MSRV and cargo-deny jobs) must be green with no deprecation annotations; a red run is yours to fix under this bead ID (`fix: <what ≤22 chars> (<this-id>)`, note appended with br before the fix commit). Release-workflow (tag) runs belong to the acceptance bead.
acceptance_criteria: Checklist 1-11 recorded; local gate incl. --locked tests, doc -D warnings, cargo deny, actionlint all exit 0; signed commit pushed; every CI job incl. MSRV and cargo-deny green with no deprecation annotations.
notes: Checklist: 1 toolchain FIXED (rust-toolchain.toml 1.93.1); 2 MSRV FIXED (CI job on 1.87.0); 3 --locked FIXED; 4 tests FIXED (--locked, doc tests); 5 docs FIXED (one rustdoc invalid_html_tags on Sort::into allowed, --help unchanged); 6 cargo-deny FIXED (all ok; CDLA-Permissive-2.0 allowed for webpki-root-certs); 7 workflow hygiene FIXED (permissions read, concurrency, checkout v7, rust-cache v2, timeouts; actionlint 0); 8 dependabot FIXED; 9 metadata FIXED (release profile pre-existing from bead 01); 10 lints table SKIPPED (would forbid unsafe set_var in tests); 11 badge deferred to 13b integration (README owned by 13b).
close_reason: Integrated by lead from parallel worktree wt/bead-rust (Sonnet worker b5d7131). Local gate on main: fmt --all, clippy --locked -D warnings, 66 tests --locked, rustdoc -D warnings, cargo deny (advisories/bans/licenses/sources ok), actionlint 0 — all green. CI with new msrv/docs/cargo-deny jobs checked after push. Dependency rewired 13d -> 12 for the parallel run.

title: 1.8 Contract: the skill teaches the 0.5.0 language
description:
Plan bead: 1.8 contract, the skill half (the documents half is hunch-7zg.8). Epic hunch-7zg.

Outcome: the skill teaches a Claude agent the language of 0.5.0: the situations that call for the output verbs, the habits, the recovery, the permissions. It teaches `jevify run`, `why -- CMD`, a shell loop over `is` and `"$(… | jevify pick …)"` today; the language replaces all four.

Context: plan §6 "Skill, for a Claude agent" and its first paragraph, vision "Where an answer is worth having". Decisions, final:
- Order for 0.5.0: the two sides (output side only), the verbs, the exit codes. The marker joins in bead 2.5 (hunch-7zg.13), where the order becomes: the two sides, the verbs, the marker, the exit codes. The skill names no verb, flag or kind that release 0.5.0 lacks: in this bead that means `why`, `pick`, `filter`, `is`, `route`, `add`, `sort`; NOT `fill`, NOT `label`, NOT `pick --from`, no marker. Bead 4.2 (hunch-7zg.20) adds label.
- Triggers for 0.5.0: a failed build over about 50 lines -> `2>&1 | jevify why`; many records, one question -> `filter`; many files, one question -> `fd -0 | jevify filter -0 --files`; one file out of many by content -> `git ls-files | jevify pick --files '…'`; the next step depends on a fact -> `is … &&`; waiting for a state -> `until … | jevify is '…'`; the long tail of a large PATH -> `route`, which only prints.
- Habits: one jevify process per question, never a loop that starts one per record; cheap tools first (grep, jq, head); yes means act; never `"$(jevify pick …)"` as an argument, because an abstention becomes an empty argument; under `git bisect run`, map exit 3 to 125. `filter -v` inverts, as `grep -v`; verbosity is `--verbose`. `is` with one statement prints nothing; read the exit code.
- Recovery: exit 2 -> copy the corrected argument; `too_many` -> grep or head; exit 4 -> the quota ("daily quota of the free backend reached") or the model, read the line.
- Permissions: allow the output verbs freely.
- The saved input (`why`, `filter`) holds the raw input, secrets included; the skill says so. `--files` withholds the excerpt of hidden files and of files that look like secrets, and says `excerpts withheld: N`.
- The frontmatter description keeps the "use when / do not use" form and drops `run` as an executor.

Files (write set): plugins/jevify/skills/jevify/SKILL.md, plugins/jevify/.claude-plugin/plugin.json, .claude-plugin/marketplace.json (descriptions only; they carry no version). Everything else is read-only; README, docs/, AGENTS.md and src/cmd/agent.rs belong to hunch-7zg.8.

Prerequisites: hunch-7zg.5 (route), hunch-bx6 (filter), hunch-7zg.6 (is), hunch-7zg.7 (pick and why): a contract bead waits for the behaviour it documents, so every status line it quotes exists on main. Copy status lines from the binary, not from the plan.

Done when:
- Every command line in the skill runs against the binary built from main (`--help` or a FakeJev run); an anchored grep over the three files finds none of: `jevify run`, `why -- `, `jevify fill`, `jevify label`, `@\{[a-z-]+:`, `pick --from`, `route --yes`, `jevify -v`.
- The text is present tense, with no meta and no retrospective language; both JSON manifests still parse (`jq . <file>`).
- The gate below passes (the documents do not change it; the worker's part of it proves the tree is green when the work is handed to the lead).

Design rules (plan §1; apply all that touch this bead):
1. Selection. Every record that pick, filter and label print is a record of the input, byte for byte. why is exempt: it points and does not reduce, so it prints each line with its number and context, as today, and takes no split option (-0, --para, --files). Every value fill substitutes is a handle that a lister printed or the caller wrote.
2. Time is the cost. A verb asks everything it can in one round, in parallel, and uses at most two rounds.
3. Asymmetric doubt. filter keeps what it is unsure about; fill and pick abstain.
4. Use the tools that exist. jevify does not do what jq, cut, grep, head, tee and cd do.
5. One role for stdin. A call never reads stdin for two purposes.

Gate, divided between the worker and the lead. Workers run in a sandbox that cannot bind 127.0.0.1 (wiremock) or reach ~/.ssh (signing).
The worker runs, from the repository root, and all must pass:
  cargo fmt --check
  cargo check --locked --all-targets
  cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings
  RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --locked --no-deps
  ubs <changed files>        # exit 0 required; verify findings, fix root causes
The worker also tries:
  cargo test --locked -- --test-threads=1
When the sandbox blocks the tests, the worker reports them as NOT RUN, with the error, never as passed. The lead then runs the full test gate outside the sandbox and sends failures back to the worker. Only the lead stages, commits (signed), pushes and closes the bead.

Rules:
- Read AGENTS.md (repository root), docs/VISION.md and the plan docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-21-jevify-two-sides.md first. The vision wins over the plan; the plan wins over this bead only where this bead is silent. Every design question of this bead is decided; nothing here waits for a decision.
- Agent Mail: register, reserve the exact write set of "Files" before the first edit (reason and thread id = this bead ID), post start and finish in that thread, release at the end. If Agent Mail is down, stop and report.
- Workers never run `git add`, `git commit`, `git push` or `br close`. The worker's last act is the finish message in the bead's thread: the files changed, the gate lines run with their results, the tests as passed or NOT RUN, scratch files left in place. The lead runs the tests, stages only the paths of "Files", commits, pushes and closes the bead.
- The tracker: a worker changes bead state with `br update` only (status, notes). Never stage, commit or edit .beads/, and never run `br sync` or `br close`. The lead exports (`br sync --flush-only`) and commits .beads/ between waves.
- One shared checkout on main. No worktree, no branch, no scratch clone, no PR. Changes of other agents in the tree are normal: never stash, revert or overwrite them.
- Never delete or rename a file. Never rm, rmdir, unlink, git rm, git stash, git restore, git reset, git clean, cargo clean, find -delete. Overwrite with an editor or write a new file. Leave scratch files in place and list them in the report. A blocked command is skipped and recorded, never routed around. Never trigger a confirmation prompt; use non-interactive flags.
- Edit code by hand, never with a script. No compatibility shim, no wrapper for a removed API, no file variants (x_v2.rs).
- For the lead's commit: only the paths of "Files" (`git commit -m "..." -- <paths>`). Subject: "<feat|fix|refactor|docs|test|chore>: <summary> (<this bead ID>)", under 72 characters. No Co-Authored-By, no session trailer. Commits are SSH-signed; never bypass signing or hooks. A new crate needs a one-line justification in the commit body; this plan adds no dependency.
- The repository is public. Before a push the lead runs: gitleaks git . --log-opts="origin/main..HEAD" --redact -v, then reads git diff origin/main..HEAD for keys, tokens, pasted API responses, absolute local paths, session URLs and personal details. On a hit, fix forward; never rewrite history, never force-push. The worker keeps all of that out of the files it writes. No communications drafts in the repository, in a bead or in a commit message.
- Never weaken, #[ignore] or delete a test to pass the gate. No live network in the default test run. Live tests (tests/live.rs) without a key are reported as NOT RUN, never as passed. Never read, print or copy a key; point jevify at it with TYPESAFE_API_KEY_FILE only.
- Rust: edition 2024, #![deny(unsafe_code)], no `set_var` in src/ (an environment a test needs is a parameter, passed through Command::env), tokio current-thread only, blocking work through spawn_blocking or std::thread::scope, argv as OsString end to end. Verify third-party APIs against docs.rs or the crate source.
- No language feature newer than Rust 1.87 (no let chains). Before the commit also run `RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --locked --no-deps`. After the lead pushes, CI runs on Linux with toolchain 1.87.0; a red CI on your commit is yours to fix forward.
- Documents state what jevify does, in the present tense, with no meta language ("this guide", "captured on") and no retrospective language ("now", "new in", "since 0.x"). History goes to CHANGELOG.md only. User-facing documents say TYPESAFE_API_KEY_FILE=/path/to/key.
- The agent-facing contract: exit codes 0 ok, 1 no, 2 usage, 3 abstain, 4 unavailable, 5 auth, 6 input, 7 child failed, 130 declined; one envelope {ok, command, version, exit_code, data, meta, error{kind, message, hint, example}}; error kinds are stable identifiers. A new verb updates cli.rs, dispatch, capabilities(), docs/ROBOT_MODE.md, README, a PRIVACY.md row and tests; in this plan the phase skeleton bead does cli.rs and dispatch, and the phase contract bead does the rest.
- A file outside "Files" is read-only. If the work needs a change there, stop, post in the thread, and let the owner of that file (named in "Files") make it.
- The `ubs` gate when the changed files are only Markdown or JSON: run `ubs <changed files>`; when it reports that nothing was scanned, record "ubs: not applicable, nothing scanned" in the bead and validate every JSON file with `jq .`. That is a pass. Any file ubs does scan (Rust, shell, Python) must still exit 0.
notes: Worker implementation complete in the three permitted paths. PASSED: cargo fmt --check; cargo check --locked --all-targets; cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings; RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --locked --no-deps. ubs: not applicable, nothing scanned (exit 3); both manifests pass jq. Twelve shell examples and inline forms pass binary --help checks; forbidden grammar scan has zero matches; Ruby Psych validates frontmatter. Full test and --lib attempts are sandbox-blocked by non-UTF-8 fixture creation: Operation not permitted (os error 1). Supplemental run excludes only that blocked fixture: all remaining 82 unit tests pass, then wiremock fails to bind an OS port (PermissionDenied). Full integration and live tests are NOT RUN. No test source changed. Skill quick_validate cannot start because Python yaml is absent; Psych validation passes instead. Excerpts-withheld status confirmed from binary; quota wording verified in source and passing client unit test, not a live quota response. Agent Mail registration and exact reservations succeeded, but message authentication was rejected by automatic approval review; unauthenticated posting also fails. No independent scratch files created; test fixtures and UBS scratch are retained. Lead must run unsandboxed full gate, commit, push, and close.
close_reason: Skill and plugin manifests teach the 0.5.0 language. ubs: not applicable, nothing scanned (Markdown and JSON). Lead gate outside the sandbox: fmt, clippy -D warnings, full cargo test --locked (18 suites pass, 4 live tests NOT RUN); JSON files validate with jq; anchored greps find no removed or future form.

title: Secret, private-info and PII audit before release
description:
Outcome: Before v0 is tagged and released, the public repo `tpellet/hunch` is audited end to end for secrets, private information and PII: a full-history gitleaks scan, a manual review of every tracked file and of the commit history, a check that no launch draft lives in the repo, a check that the release config and the locally built installer carry no local paths, and a check that user-facing docs use the generic key path and no personal tooling details. Fix-forward findings are fixed in this bead; anything that would need a history rewrite or a key rotation is recorded, never rewritten, and blocks v0 acceptance pending Thomas. The verdict is a short pass/fail note in the close reason with no secret value quoted. Lead-added (Thomas, 2026-09-19: "before the push to public remote we check for any secret/any private information and PII that should not be shared"); the lead's own audit of the pre-code history (2026-09-19) found SECRET 0, and the lead's authorized history rewrite of 2026-09-19 removed the low PRIVATE items, so the pre-code baseline is clean (17 commits at 5ed92d6).

Read first: ~/.claude/AGENTS.md ("## Public Repositories — Push With Care") and /Users/tpellet/Projects/hunch/AGENTS.md (every time); the plan docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-18-hunch-v0.md — "## Global Constraints" and "### Task 16: Release — binaries, launch checklist (Homebrew tap and Show HN optional, user-gated)" Step 2b; `.gitleaks.toml` (hunch-task-01-scaffold-p8n); README.md, PRIVACY.md, docs/ROBOT_MODE.md, CHANGELOG.md, benchmarks/results.md as shipped.

Context:
- Scope: everything reachable from `git log --all` plus every tracked file at HEAD (`git ls-files`), including `.beads/issues.jsonl` (descriptions, notes, close reasons), `evals/` (inventory, eval outputs, prototype files), `benchmarks/` (results, fixtures), `docs/`, the dist config and `.github/workflows/`. Ignored local files (`.beads/beads.db*`, `evals/out/`, `target/`) are not published and are out of scope, but confirm they are still ignored (`git status --ignored | head`).
- Step 1, scanners (outside the sandbox): `gitleaks version` (8.30.1 installed; `brew install gitleaks` if missing); `gitleaks git . --log-opts="--all" --redact -v --report-path "$TMPDIR/gl-git.json"` and `gitleaks dir . --redact -v --report-path "$TMPDIR/gl-dir.json"`; both must print "no leaks found". A finding that is a real credential value: record the file, commit and rule id only (never the value), do not fix by rewriting, go to Step 6.
- Step 2, manual pattern sweep over `git log --all -p` (read the matches, do not trust counts): `git log --all -p | grep -n -i -E "authorization:|bearer |sk-[a-z0-9]|ghp_|github_pat_|api[_-]?key=|token=|/Users/|/private/tmp/|/home/|claude\.ai/code/session|@gmail\.com|@[a-z0-9-]+\.(com|ai|io)"`; every hit is classified BENIGN (placeholder such as `TYPESAFE_API_KEY=test-key`, the commit author's own email in doc text, a public URL), PRIVATE (a local path, a session URL, a private repo or project name, personal tooling) or SECRET (a value). The commit author identity (name and email) on commits is Thomas's chosen public identity: BENIGN. Absolute paths inside internal files — bead descriptions, notes and close reasons, the plan, AGENTS.md (the checkout /Users/tpellet/Projects/hunch, the launch folder /Users/tpellet/Projects/hunch-launch/, the skill paths under /Users/tpellet/.claude/skills/) — are instructions: classify BENIGN-internal, no action. Only user-facing docs, code, benchmarks/, eval outputs and release artifacts must be free of them.
- Step 3, tracked-file review, one file at a time, by eye: README.md, PRIVACY.md, docs/ROBOT_MODE.md, CHANGELOG.md, benchmarks/README.md, benchmarks/results.md, evals/inventory.json (tool names from this machine are a light fingerprint: BENIGN, keep), evals/prototype/*, docs/superpowers/**, AGENTS.md, `.beads/issues.jsonl` (every `notes` and `close_reason`: no pasted API response, no draft sentence, no value), and every commit message body (`git log --format='%H%n%B' origin/main`). title: Task 3: Jev client with retries, concurrency, disk cache, prewarm
description:
Outcome: The Jev HTTP client (`Client::new/ask/prewarm`) with retries, a concurrency semaphore and a blake3-keyed 7-day disk cache; the shared test harness `tests/common/mod.rs` (FakeJev over wiremock, `bin()`, `hunch()`, `config()`, `option_containing()`); `tests/client.rs` (3 tests) and the 2 inline unit tests of `jev/client.rs` (`retry_after`, `rejection_message`) pass; committed and pushed.

Read first: ~/.claude/AGENTS.md and /Users/tpellet/Projects/hunch/AGENTS.md (every time); the spec docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-18-hunch-v0-design.md; the plan docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-18-hunch-v0.md — "## Global Constraints" and the section "### Task 3: Jev client with retries, concurrency, disk cache, prewarm" (Steps 1–5). The plan holds the verbatim, compile-verified code; copy it exactly, do not redesign. Run `cargo fmt` before `cargo fmt --check`.

Context:
- Consumes (Task 2): `config::Config` (pub fields; `api_key()`, `base_url`, `model`, `concurrency`, `cache_dir`, `stats`), `jev::{Questions, Response}`, `jev::client::Stats` (already in client.rs — append the client below it), `HunchError`. What the verbatim `tests/client.rs` calls, so a compile error can be told from Task 2 drift: `Config::meta() -> Meta` (reads `stats.cache_hits` and `stats.request_id` into `Meta.cache_hits` / `Meta.request_id`), `Question::noul(impl Into<String>)`, `Questions::new()` (a map), `Response::noul(&self, id) -> Result<f64, HunchError>`, `HunchError::{exit() -> Exit, kind() -> &str}` with `RejectedRequest(u16, String)` displaying `HTTP <status>`; `jev/mod.rs` (Task 2) already declares `pub mod cache; pub mod client;` and `cache.rs` is the one-line stub `// Implemented in Task 3.`

title: Task 10: hunch run argument pointing, never-execute list, confirmation, execution, init
description:
Outcome: `hunch run` is complete: argument pointing from man-page flags and tokens copied from the request (`src/args.rs`), the never-execute list by tool name/prefix, `/dev/tty` confirmation or `--yes`, machine-mode execution only with `--exec --yes` (child stdout → stderr so stdout stays one envelope), and `hunch init zsh|bash` (the `,` alias); 5 contract + 3 unit tests pass; the live smoke `live_run_routes_tar` is added and run; committed and pushed.

Read first: ~/.claude/AGENTS.md and /Users/tpellet/Projects/hunch/AGENTS.md (every time); the spec docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-18-hunch-v0-design.md; the plan docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-18-hunch-v0.md — "## Global Constraints" (Safety bullet) and the section "### Task 10: `hunch run` — argument pointing, never-execute list, confirmation, execution, shell alias" (Design paragraph, Execution policy, Steps 1–7). The plan holds the verbatim, compile-verified code; copy it exactly, do not redesign. Run `cargo fmt` before `cargo fmt --check`.

Context:
- Consumes: Task 9 `cmd::run::{route, Route, RunFlags, load_tools}`; `manpage::{Flag, options_text, parse_flags}`, `inventory::Tool` (Task 8); `jev::client::Client`, `jev::{Question, Questions}`, `Response.answers` (Tasks 2–3); `cmd::confirm_tty` (Task 1, the shared prompt), `cli::Shell`, `cmd::Outcome`, `Exit`, `HunchError::{Declined, Input}`; `tests/live.rs::live_key_present` (Task 8); harness `common::{mock, hunch, bin, FakeJev, option_containing}`.
- Produces: `args::value_candidates(request: &str) -> Vec<String>` (quoted strings first, then tokens containing a digit, `.`, `/` or `~`, trailing `,.:` trimmed, deduped, ≤ 40); `args::Proposal { argv: Vec<String>, flags: Vec<(String, f64)>, file: Option<(String, f64)>, placeholders: usize }`; `async args::propose(client, request, tool: &Tool, flags: &[Flag], cwd: &[String], threshold: f64) -> Result<Proposal, HunchError>` (ONE request: state `{ request, tool, flags: ["--x — desc"], values: ["[V00] v"], files: ["[F000] f"] }`; per flag i a Noul `use{i:03}` ("Does `request` ask for the behaviour described in `flags[{i}]`?" — what the request is, never whether a flag should be passed), per value-taking flag a Choice `val{i:03}` over V-ids + NONE, one Choice `file` over F-ids + NONE; keep flags whose Noul `p >= threshold.max(FLAG_FLOOR)`; value from the chosen V-id else the placeholder `<VALUE>` (placeholders += 1); file appended only if its Choice `p >= threshold.max(FILE_FLOOR)`; order tool, flags in help order, file; missing Noul answers are `Protocol` errors via `?`). At the top of src/args.rs, `const FLAG_FLOOR: f64 = 0.7; const FILE_FLOOR: f64 = 0.6;` with the plan's doc comment: floors above the user's threshold for composing argv, a higher-stakes step than routing — raising `-t` tightens both, lowering it never loosens them (Global Constraints: the threshold gates absolute Nouls; a Choice probability is never compared to it directly, and the file floor is the one documented exception, as a floor). - Execution policy (copy exactly): `!flags.no_args` → parse flags via `spawn_blocking(manpage::parse_flags(&manpage::options_text(&name).unwrap_or_default()))`, list cwd (non-hidden names), `files = relevant_files(intent, &cwd)`, and call `args::propose` only if flags or files are non-empty; `complete = placeholders == 0`; `blocked = blocked_reason(&tool.name)`; human mode prints on stderr: the route line when `--dry-run`, each chosen flag with its man-page description, and "hunch: fill the <VALUE> placeholders and run it yourself:" or "hunch: not offering to run this (<why>); check it and run it yourself:"; `may_execute = complete && blocked.is_none() && !dry_run && (machine ? exec && yes : yes || confirm_tty(prompt)? == Some(true))`, where `Some(false)` → `Err(HunchError::Declined)` (exit 130) and `None` (no TTY) → print only, exit 0; execution via `std::process::Command::new(&argv[0]).args(&argv[1..])` (argv only, never a shell), with `child.stdout(std::io::stderr())` in machine mode; `.status()`; exit `ChildFailed` (7) iff executed and child code ≠ 0; human stdout = `argv.join(" ") + "\n"` unless executed. title: Sufficiency gate: ask whether the evidence is enough before asking which one
description:
Workflow from a Jev practitioner's measured tip (2026-09-20, JEV TIP 005): an 'I don't know' option inside a Choice does not work (it won 0 of 80 runs, because it mixes 'which one' with 'is there enough evidence'), and a Choice over a state that supports two answers flips with option order. A separate Noul, 'does the state hold enough decision-relevant evidence to answer this question', was stable: 38.75 to 38.95 percent, and reversing the order moved it by 0.20 points. Rule: calibrate a sufficiency threshold on labelled examples, ask the intent question only above it, otherwise get more evidence and ask again.

In jevify: (1) compare the present any Noul of tournament::window ('is at least one entry the thing described') with a sufficiency wording, on the held-out queries of the operand experiment; (2) evidence escalation: handle line first, richer evidence (commit body, file excerpt, pod status) only when sufficiency is low, as a declared second evidence level of a source; dogfood case in hunch-1qa: git log --oneline lacks the commit body and pick exits 3; (3) a distinct abstention for agents, error kind insufficient_evidence with a hint that names the evidence to add, apart from no_match; (4) the round budget: sufficiency and Choice can share one request, an escalation is a new decision level and needs the AGENTS.md wording on rounds; (5) the measured sufficiency value sat far from 0.5, so the one-threshold principle needs a per-question-type calibration answer (feeds hunch-o88). Gate: numbers from recorded runs on both backends; no claim of calibration without labelled examples. Part of epic hunch-4z4.
notes:
Owner, 2026-09-20: the sufficiency question also works when asked AFTER the intent question. Three placements to measure on the same held-out set: (a) before: gate whether to ask at all, cheapest on poor evidence and the trigger for evidence escalation; (b) alongside, in the same request: no extra latency, but it cannot name the winner because the Choice result is not known yet (this is where today's any Noul sits); (c) after, conditioned on the winner: 'does the state hold enough evidence that <winner> is the thing described', candidate-specific, which closes the gap found in review (pick, why and sort confirm that something fits, never that the winner fits; run already confirms per candidate). For a domain of one window, (a or b) plus (c) stays inside two rounds. Report accepted precision, coverage and requests for each placement.
Deferred per docs/VISION.md: fill and pick start with Choice plus NONE and the margin check. Evidence tiers stay; the any/enough Noul pair returns only if dogfooding shows wrong picks on thin evidence.
close_reason: Superseded by docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-21-jevify-two-sides.md (epic hunch-7zg): the guards are NONE, the any Noul, the ratio p(best) >= 2 x max(p(second), p(NONE)) and the insufficient_evidence budget check (section 2.1 step 5); no separate sufficiency round.

title: Evaluate run for agents on tools the model cannot know
description: The pilot in benchmarks/agents/ only needed tools a frontier model knows by name, so it could not show whether run helps an agent. Test the case it is built for. Design: a scratch bin directory on PATH and MANPATH with invented internal CLIs (neutral names that do not reveal their function, each with a man page and a script that records a correct invocation), mixed into the real PATH of about 2,000 commands. A multi-step job stated as outcomes. Arms: plain agent versus agent with skills/grevi/SKILL.md, 5 or more runs per arm, same model. Both arms are told internal tools exist on PATH, neither is told their names. Measure: steps passed by the checker, tokens, tool calls, wall time, and how each agent discovered the tool (apropos, man -k, ls, grevi run). Also measure at two inventory sizes (tens and hundreds of internal tools), because the alternative to run is reading man-page summaries and that cost grows with the inventory. Report whatever comes out. If run loses, find out why (routing, flags, latency) and feed hunch-eil. Gate: checker script plus results in benchmarks/agents/, numbers only from recorded runs.
notes:
Use benchmarks/agents/EXPERIMENT.md as the experiment contract. This issue supplies the unfamiliar-tool run cohort for hunch-ric/hunch-evl; the earlier five-runs suggestion is a smoke test, not a powered performance claim. Preserve familiar-tool controls, identical discovery permissions and actual executable outcomes.
Lowered per docs/VISION.md (hunch-vq2): build fill, filter and label first; measurement follows use.

title: 2.2 Pool rule: one finalists rule (3, 2, 1 by rank) for every caller of tournament::rank
description:
Plan bead: 2.2, the pool-rule half — src/tournament.rs (the source half of 2.2 is hunch-q8p, which writes src/source.rs). Epic hunch-7zg. This bead replaces the earlier "measure candidate survival" framing with the rule the plan fixes; the measurement is the evaluation that follows the language (hunch-lpp).

Outcome: a long list is searched in two rounds without ever comparing a probability from one request with one from another, and without cutting the pool: the right candidate in any window reaches the finals. One rule serves every caller of `tournament::rank`: `fill`, stdin `pick`, `pick --from` and `why`.

Context: plan §2.1 (the paragraph "One pool rule for every caller" with its table, steps 4 and 5), §2 "Changed in place" (src/tournament.rs), §8.1, §9.4; vision "A long list is searched in two rounds". Today src/tournament.rs:126-127 sorts the finalists of all windows by probability and truncates to 24 (`MAX_FINALISTS`), which compares probabilities across requests. Decisions, final:
- W is the window of the backend: 200 candidates on TypeSafe, 99 on classifier.dev (`Backend::window`, src/config.rs:34). F = W x (W / 3): 13,200 and 3,267.
- ONE RULE for every caller of `tournament::rank`: finalists per window `n` = 3 when `3 x windows <= W`, else 2 when `2 x windows <= W`, else 1. Always by rank inside a window, never by a probability from another request. Capacity is `W x W` candidates (9,801 keyless; on TypeSafe the 20,000 ceiling is reached first).
- `fill` uses `n = 3` only, so its limit stays `F = W x (W / 3)`: the caller passes a mode (for example `Finalists::ThreeOnly` against `Finalists::Auto`), and above F in that mode `rank` returns the capacity error with no request.
- `pick`, `pick --from` and `why` use the full rule. Above `W x W`: an ordered list keeps its newest `W x W` and the status line says so; any other list is exit 6 `too_many` (narrow with `grep`, `head` or a prefix). stdin `pick` allows 20,000 lines today (`MAX_LINES`, src/cmd/pick.rs:9): its stdin list is not ordered, so on the classifier backend 9,802 lines are `too_many` with no request; `MAX_LINES` stays as the second bound (it is the first one reached on TypeSafe).
- `why` keeps `MAX_KEEP = 4000` (src/cmd/why.rs:13): 41 windows keyless, n = 2, 82 finalists in one finals request. `why` needs no capacity error: 4,000 is below 9,801.
- The two statements of the earlier text, "callers keep their behaviour" and "never compare across requests", cannot both hold for 41 windows; the second wins. The behaviour that stays is the contract of each verb (exit codes, envelope, output format), not the identity of the 24 finalists.
- The API keeps its shape; finalist evidence needs no callback ("a closure or a second slice" is gone). A caller with tier-two evidence makes two calls: `shortlist` (round 1, :149), then it fetches the evidence of the finalists itself (async, inside spawn_blocking, after the withholding check), then `window` (:55, `pub(crate)` since hunch-7zg.7; keep that) for the finals. `fill`, `pick --from` and `pick --files` use these two calls. `rank` stays for callers with no tier two (stdin `pick`, `why`), and it KEEPS its `finalist_text` parameter for `why`: `why` is its remaining user (src/cmd/why.rs:116-122 passes `Some(&with_context)`, so the finals carry each line with its context lines, and a one-window `why` still sends two requests, src/tournament.rs:110); stdin `pick` passes `None` (src/cmd/pick.rs:87). The pool rule applies to both paths: `rank` internally, and `shortlist`, whose `per_window` becomes the `n` of the rule (it reports `windows` and `n`); `pick --files`, which cut its shortlist to 24 in src/cmd/pick.rs since hunch-7zg.7 (`MAX_FINALISTS`, :10, and the `truncate` at :62-64), moves to the rule here. `route` passes its own `per_window` and asks its own absolute second question; it stays as it is.
- THE FINALIST ORDER is defined once, here, and hunch-bkb and hunch-7zg.12 use it: by rank, then by window index (rank 1 of every window in window order, then rank 2 of every window, then rank 3). No probability from one request is compared with one from another to build it. "Tier-two evidence for the first 24" (`MAX_FINALISTS`) means the first 24 of that order, so every window's best candidate gets tier-two evidence before any window's second.
- `shortlist` returns the per-window `Ranking`s (candidates, `any`, `none`), not only candidates, and alongside them the finalists in the order above (for example `struct Shortlist { windows: Vec<Ranking>, finalists: Vec<Candidate>, n: usize }`); today src/tournament.rs:149-167 flattens the windows, sorts them by probability (:166) and discards `any` and `none`. With ONE window the caller decides from that `Ranking` (through `decide`) with no second request. `route` calls `shortlist` at src/cmd/run.rs:42 and then takes `.take(12)` over a pool sorted by probability across windows; that is `route`'s own, present behaviour and it stays: the adapter in src/cmd/run.rs re-flattens the windows' candidates, sorts them by probability and keeps its `take(12)`.
- The tier-two evidence of the finalists comes from `source::enrich(kind, handles)` (hunch-q8p), called by `fill` and `pick --from` between `shortlist` and `window`; tournament.rs never calls it.
- Round 1: one `window` per W candidates (one Choice with NONE, one `any` Noul), all in flight at the same time.
- Round 2, one request: with several windows it is the finals: the `n` best of each window BY RANK, all of them, with tier-two evidence for the first 24 of the finalist order (`MAX_FINALISTS` bounds tier-two evidence only, not the pool). With one window, round 2 runs only when the ratio failed and the kind has tier-two evidence: this one-window shortcut applies to `fill` and `pick --from` (their callers decide it, since they make the two calls); `pick --files` always runs round two, as today. Never a third round.
- `decide(&Ranking, threshold: f64)` (tournament.rs has no `Config`; the caller passes `ctx.threshold`): found when `any >= threshold` and `p(best) >= 2 x max(p(second), p(NONE))`. A ratio holds for 3 options and for 200. Equal scores abstain. The factor is a constant in tournament.rs; there is no setting for it. `decide` returns found / no_match / ambiguous with the two closest candidates, for the status lines of `fill` and `pick --from`. `decide` serves `fill` and `pick --from` ONLY: stdin `pick` keeps its present found rule (`any >= threshold` and best > NONE, src/cmd/pick.rs:89-94) and its `-n N` semantics; `why` keeps its own rule.
- tournament.rs does no I/O. The `Ranking` reports `windows` and `n`, so a caller prints `finalists per window: 2` when n is not 3.
- `why`, `pick` and `route` call `rank` and `shortlist` today (imports: src/cmd/why.rs:5, src/cmd/pick.rs:6, src/cmd/run.rs:8; calls: src/cmd/why.rs:116, src/cmd/pick.rs:62 and :87, src/cmd/run.rs:42). Adapt the call sites of `rank` to the new signature, make stdin `pick` map the capacity error to exit 6 `too_many`, and print the `finalists per window` line. `shortlist` (src/tournament.rs:149) keeps every window's top `per_window` and cuts nothing (the sort by probability at :166 orders, it does not truncate; it leaves with this bead, replaced by the finalist order above). It gains the mode of the rule (`Finalists::ThreeOnly`, `Finalists::Auto`, or the fixed `per_window` that `route` passes today) and the capacity error. `route` asks its own absolute second question and keeps its behaviour; src/cmd/run.rs is touched only for the changed signature.

Files (write set): src/tournament.rs, tests/tournament.rs; call-site adaptation and the capacity behaviour in src/cmd/why.rs, src/cmd/pick.rs, src/cmd/run.rs, with their contract tests in tests/pick.rs and tests/why.rs (added tests only). Everything else is read-only (tests/common/mod.rs gives probability vectors per question since bead 1.2). For the classifier backend, tests/tournament.rs builds a literal `jevify::config::Config { backend: Backend::Classifier, key: None, base_url: server.uri(), … }` against `common::mock_classifier` (tests/common/mod.rs:274), because `common::config()` builds a TypeSafe config only (tests/common/mod.rs:335-348) and that file is read-only here. hunch-7zg.12 (`pick --from`) writes src/cmd/pick.rs and tests/pick.rs after this bead; hunch-q8p runs in parallel and shares no file.

Prerequisites: hunch-7zg.10.

Done when, as tests:
- 250 candidates resolve in two rounds and the finals request holds three finalists of every window (inspect the captured request).
- The rule: for W = 99, 33 windows give n = 3, 34 give n = 2, 49 give n = 2, 50 give n = 1, 99 give n = 1; the same boundaries for W = 200 (66/67, 100/101).
- Classifier backend, 4,000 items: 41 windows, n = 2, one finals request with 82 finalists, the planted answer wins. Classifier backend, 9,802 items: the capacity error, no request; through stdin `pick` that is exit 6 `too_many` with the ways to narrow (tests/pick.rs); 9,801 items resolve with n = 1.
- `why` with `MAX_KEEP` kept lines on the classifier backend resolves in two rounds with n = 2 (tests/why.rs), and its output format is unchanged.
- `why` keeps `finalist_text` (tests/why.rs, inspect the captured requests): the finals request still carries the context lines of each finalist (`context only, not a candidate; before: …`), and a `why` whose lines fit ONE window still sends two requests.
- The finalist order: with 3 windows and n = 3, the finals request lists rank 1 of windows 0, 1, 2, then rank 2 of each, then rank 3 of each, whatever the round-one probabilities; `shortlist` returns the finalists in that order next to the per-window `Ranking`s. `route` over several windows still takes its 12 by probability (tests/run_route.rs stays green, read-only).
- `ThreeOnly` (fill): F candidates resolve; F + 1 is the capacity error with no request.
- The right candidate in the last window wins even when another window's finalists have higher round-one probabilities.
- Two close rivals in one window both reach the finals and end as `ambiguous`; a tie abstains; NONE close to the best abstains; `any` below the threshold is `no_match`.
- `shortlist` with one window, then `decide` on its `Ranking`, each with EXACTLY ONE request: a decisive winner is found; a low `any` is `no_match`; a dominant `NONE` is `no_match`.
- Classifier backend, 9,802 candidates: an unordered list is the capacity error (`too_many` at the caller) with no request; for an ordered kind the caller trims to the newest 9,801 before calling and says so (that trim is the caller's, hunch-7zg.12; here: 9,801 resolve).
- `decide` as a pure function: the ratio holds, the ratio fails, equal scores, NONE close to the best, `any` below the threshold. The one-window shortcut itself is tested by its callers (hunch-bkb, hunch-7zg.12). stdin `pick` with a best that beats NONE but fails the ratio is still found (its rule is unchanged), and `-n 3` still prints three.
- `pick --files` above one window follows the pool rule (the 24-cut of src/cmd/pick.rs is gone) and still always runs round two.
- W, W + 1, F candidates on each backend: the request counts are 1, 2 + 1, and W/3 windows + 1.
- A deterministic 1,800-item regression: the planted answer survives in every position of every window.
- Existing why, pick and route suites stay green; a test that asserted the old 24-finalist pool is rewritten to the rule above and the finish message names it, for the lead's commit body (this is the decided rule, not a weakened test).
- The gate below passes.

Design rules (plan §1; apply all that touch this bead):
1. Selection. Every record that pick, filter and label print is a record of the input, byte for byte. why is exempt: it points and does not reduce, so it prints each line with its number and context, as today, and takes no split option (-0, --para, --files). Every value fill substitutes is a handle that a lister printed or the caller wrote.
2. Time is the cost. A verb asks everything it can in one round, in parallel, and uses at most two rounds.
3. Asymmetric doubt. filter keeps what it is unsure about; fill and pick abstain.
4. Use the tools that exist. jevify does not do what jq, cut, grep, head, tee and cd do.
5. One role for stdin. A call never reads stdin for two purposes.

Gate, divided between the worker and the lead. Workers run in a sandbox that cannot bind 127.0.0.1 (wiremock) or reach ~/.ssh (signing).
The worker runs, from the repository root, and all must pass:
  cargo fmt --check
  cargo check --locked --all-targets
  cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings
  RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --locked --no-deps
  ubs <changed files>        # exit 0 required; verify findings, fix root causes
The worker also tries:
  cargo test --locked -- --test-threads=1
When the sandbox blocks the tests, the worker reports them as NOT RUN, with the error, never as passed. The lead then runs the full test gate outside the sandbox and sends failures back to the worker. Only the lead stages, commits (signed), pushes and closes the bead.

Rules:
- Read AGENTS.md (repository root), docs/VISION.md and the plan docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-21-jevify-two-sides.md first. The vision wins over the plan; the plan wins over this bead only where this bead is silent. Every design question of this bead is decided; nothing here waits for a decision.
- Agent Mail: register, reserve the exact write set of "Files" before the first edit (reason and thread id = this bead ID), post start and finish in that thread, release at the end. If Agent Mail is down, stop and report.
- Workers never run `git add`, `git commit`, `git push` or `br close`. The worker's last act is the finish message in the bead's thread: the files changed, the gate lines run with their results, the tests as passed or NOT RUN, scratch files left in place. The lead runs the tests, stages only the paths of "Files", commits, pushes and closes the bead.
- The tracker: a worker changes bead state with `br update` only (status, notes). Never stage, commit or edit .beads/, and never run `br sync` or `br close`. The lead exports (`br sync --flush-only`) and commits .beads/ between waves.
- One shared checkout on main. No worktree, no branch, no scratch clone, no PR. Changes of other agents in the tree are normal: never stash, revert or overwrite them.
- Never delete or rename a file. Never rm, rmdir, unlink, git rm, git stash, git restore, git reset, git clean, cargo clean, find -delete. Overwrite with an editor or write a new file. Leave scratch files in place and list them in the report. A blocked command is skipped and recorded, never routed around. Never trigger a confirmation prompt; use non-interactive flags.
- Edit code by hand, never with a script. No compatibility shim, no wrapper for a removed API, no file variants (x_v2.rs).
- For the lead's commit: only the paths of "Files" (`git commit -m "..." -- <paths>`). Subject: "<feat|fix|refactor|docs|test|chore>: <summary> (<this bead ID>)", under 72 characters. No Co-Authored-By, no session trailer. Commits are SSH-signed; never bypass signing or hooks. A new crate needs a one-line justification in the commit body; this plan adds no dependency.
- The repository is public. Before a push the lead runs: gitleaks git . --log-opts="origin/main..HEAD" --redact -v, then reads git diff origin/main..HEAD for keys, tokens, pasted API responses, absolute local paths, session URLs and personal details. On a hit, fix forward; never rewrite history, never force-push. The worker keeps all of that out of the files it writes. No communications drafts in the repository, in a bead or in a commit message.
- Never weaken, #[ignore] or delete a test to pass the gate. No live network in the default test run. Live tests (tests/live.rs) without a key are reported as NOT RUN, never as passed. Never read, print or copy a key; point jevify at it with TYPESAFE_API_KEY_FILE only.
- Rust: edition 2024, #![deny(unsafe_code)], no `set_var` in src/ (an environment a test needs is a parameter, passed through Command::env), tokio current-thread only, blocking work through spawn_blocking or std::thread::scope, argv as OsString end to end. - Documents state what jevify does, in the present tense, with no meta language ("this guide", "captured on") and no retrospective language ("now", "new in", "since 0.x"). History goes to CHANGELOG.md only. User-facing documents say TYPESAFE_API_KEY_FILE=/path/to/key.
- The agent-facing contract: exit codes 0 ok, 1 no, 2 usage, 3 abstain, 4 unavailable, 5 auth, 6 input, 7 child failed, 130 declined; one envelope {ok, command, version, exit_code, data, meta, error{kind, message, hint, example}}; error kinds are stable identifiers. A new verb updates cli.rs, dispatch, capabilities(), docs/ROBOT_MODE.md, README, a PRIVACY.md row and tests; in this plan the phase skeleton bead does cli.rs and dispatch, and the phase contract bead does the rest.
